Little do they realize that before the skull is even formed, the original eye is already clear. With a single "pwa" sound, everything is resolved once and for all.

Even so, those who have attained personal realization are not one or two in ten thousand, while those who have misunderstood are as numerous as the sands of the Ganges. A verse on the Buddha’s Enlightenment says: Six years of snow...
Just as he was about to attain the Way on the mountain pass, he struck and lost the eyes of his former ghost.
With his face full of shame and having no place to hide, he has been terrified of seeing the morning star ever since.
Chan Master Deyin of Xuefeng at Fuzhou composed a eulogy for Pūbaguo (Bagua) Bodhisattva, saying: "A staff over his shoulder..."
A cloth bag wanders through the dusty world; when has this matter ever been seen intimately? Consciousness of karma is vast and boundless, with no foundation to rely upon;
not knowing who it is that one laughs at when opening one's mouth.
Continued Collection of the Record of the Transmission of the Lamp, Volume II and Volume III.
Compiled by the former abbot of Jingshan Xingsheng Wanshou Chan Monastery, the bhikṣu Wénxiù of Wúxún.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Lingyin Songyuan Yue (20th generation after Dajian Huineng):
Chan Master Mingweng Wenli of Tiantong, Mingzhou. He was a native of Lin’an, Hangzhou, and his family resided at Mount Tianmu.
At the foot of this mountain, it was therefore also called Tianmu. His surname was Shen. When the Master was six years old, he followed his mother with a basket to gather mulberry leaves.
Suddenly, he woke from a dream and thought to himself, "Who is it that carries this basket? Thereupon, he resolved to leave the household life.

At the age of sixteen, he went to Zhenxiang Temple in his hometown and received the tonsure under the monk Zhimue. He traveled to Jingci Temple to study under Hunyuan, but they did not reach a mutual accord, so he went to visit Yuyang.
Chan Master Fozhao Guang was asked by Zhao, "As you come in this manner, which one is your true host? The Master suddenly attained realization of the meaning.
On another day, Zhao asked again, "Regarding that monk who said, 'It is the wind moving, it is the banner moving'—what did he mean? The Master replied:
When the object was seen by the Master, his eyes stood out wide. Again he asked, "It is neither the wind moving nor the banner moving;
where do you see the Patriarch? The Master replied, "Lift off the skull-cap. Zhaoxi, greatly impressed by his brilliance and elegance, took him as his secretary.

After some time, he returned to Zhejiang to hear the principles of the "Threefold Contemplation in One Mind" at Shangzhu. At that time, Songyuan was propagating the Way at Jianfu in Raoyang. [The room...]
Zhong asked a monk, "It is not the wind moving; it is not the banner moving. As soon as the monk hesitated, Zhong struck him with his staff and drove him out.

Upon hearing this, the Master (Dongshan) suddenly forgot all his intellectual understanding and went to study under him. Having received formal approval (*inka*), he took leave to travel through the Jianghuai region to pay homage at the ancestral shrines.
Upon arriving at Mount Jiang, Master Zhe’ung appointed him as the Head Seat for Ordination. You Gong Yu, a native of Jinling, frequently visited the mountain to listen to the Master’s discourses;

he was deeply moved and won over by them. In the fifth year of the Jiading era, the layman Zhang Gong Yi of Yuezhai invited him to open a dharma seat at Huiyun Monastery, after which he moved to Nengren Monastery in Wenzhou.
Not long thereafter, he retired to Xiqiu in Qiantang. [There,] Yue Gong Jiezhai...
Admiring the Master’s lofty conduct, he traveled incognito to Xiqiu. The Master did not inquire after his name, yet they conversed all day before he departed.
The following day, he submitted a memorial requesting that the Master take up residence as abbot of Jingci. Later, he retired to Fquan and eventually resided at Tiantong.
A monk asked, "What was it like when Niutou had not yet met the Fourth Patriarch? The Master said, "Niutou. The monk asked, "After he had met him..."
“How is it? The Master said, “Ox-head, Ox-head. A monk asked, “How was it when you saw Foguo?
The Master said, “There is jade within the stone. The monk asked, “And after you saw Songyuan? The Master said, “There is no oil in the sand.

A monk asked, “Are the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, “Bamboo shoots on South Mountain; cuttlefish from the East Sea. The monk hesitated.
The Master then struck the wooden fish three times with his toothpick. He ascended the hall and said: "The long-necked crane does not perch in the lofty trees but flies crosswise beyond the heavens;
the flat-nosed ox, having finished plowing the mountain fields, goes straight up to the mountain peak. The patch-robed monks of the world cannot even hope to reach them. Why is this so?"

At Jiazhou, while striking the great statue, he ascended the hall and cited the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra*, which says: "All that can be returned is naturally not you; that which cannot be returned—if it is not you, then who is it?
The Master composed a verse: "That which cannot be returned—who else could it be? Fading red petals drift upon the fishing piers.
The sun slants, the wind has stilled, and no one sweeps them up; A swallow picks them up and flies away toward the water’s edge. [End of section]
The Hall. Master Touzi said: "If you go forward to meet him, you do not see his head; if you follow after him, you do not see his form. He is very much like Xu Liu carrying a single board.
Tiantong, however, is not so: "Looking up, he is ever higher; looking down, he is not far away. A heron at night roosts in the willow grove, taking flight askance;
several silver vases hang from the tree’s waist. Entering the hall, [he said]: "Sentient beings have never been deluded. At night..."
The rooster crows toward the fifth watch. The Buddhas have never awakened. In the clarity of autumn, wild geese pass through the vast sky.

(He strikes his knee once and says: "Last night by the western window, the moonlight was bright; the cool breeze has already reached the wutong trees. On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascends the hall and says:
"Last night, Dharma Master Kāśyapa Matanga lit lotus lamps everywhere to assist the radiance of the Buddha, until even the faithful were moved."
The Real Man lost his radiance. Taibai Dragon King came forth and said, "Since the time of the Buddha King of the Noble Seed (Ratnakoṭi), I have dwelt on this mountain;
I have never heard such news. Thereupon, he struck a flash of lightning in the sky, which transformed into a black wind and torrential rain filling the heavens.
Do you understand? I saw the lamp-lighting Buddha’s original radiant auspiciousness.

Thus it was. On the anniversary of Master Hongzhi’s passing, he ascended the hall and said: "Beyond the night-bright curtain and before the precious mirror stand, there is fundamentally nothing that is dualistic;
how could there be any partiality or completeness? At this very moment, who ultimately occupies the position of centrality?
The ancient ferry is deserted, the frosty moon is cold; the reeds are stilled by the wind, and the herons sleep. A monk came forward and entered the abbot’s quarters, saying, "I, [Name],..."
Someone came forward with a formal accusation against the Master. The Master asked, "Where is the accuser? The man replied, "The Master himself is he.
The Master said, "What grievance or enmity do I have with you? The man was speechless. The Master seized him and said, "Enemy! Enemy! A newly arrived monk came for an audience.
The Master asked, "What is your name? The monk replied, "Zhihu (Wisdom Tiger). The Master stepped back and acted as if afraid.
The monk hesitated to speak. The Master immediately returned to his quarters. Dharma Master Fuguang was the first to rely upon the Master at Liangzhu.
The Master ordered him to go to Lower Zhuyun to study under Beifeng Yinguang. He composed two verses to see him off, saying: "Return and rely upon Mount Gṛdhrakūṭa;
His house has always rejected the three preceding schools. Who would have known that after diverging, we would return to the same? The perfect principle is manifest now."
He also grew weary of talk. "Discerning the object clearly is the wondrous medicinal prescription; all other conceptual discriminations must be further forgotten.

When the evening breeze blows down the fragments of withered red petals, do not seek their former fragrance upon the branches. This has been passed down and recited in the monastic communities to this day. The Master was profound in his knowledge of the *I Ching*.

During the Qián and Chún eras, when various Confucian scholars greatly expounded the School of Daoxue, the Master associated with them, yet he directly revealed the Dharma of Mind to them rather than [engaging in conventional learning].
"Worldly talk" refers to following after and seeking to please others. When Zhu Hui-ān asked about "sincerity without deviation," the Master joined his hands to demonstrate it to him.
When Yang Cihu asked about the power of non-deception, the Master replied with a verse: "This power is clearly present in non-deception; How many people can truly understand non-deception?
If you wish to clarify the phrase that grasps both the elephant and the rabbit, Look at the moment he ascends the steps with his formal tablet upright. This was his awakening.
Such was the nature of humanity. The Master attained the five supernormal powers (*pañcābhijñā*) in no more than eight or nine years.

During that interval, he spent much of his time in leisure on the western hills by Liangzhu. When groups of monks came to seek instruction and inquiry, he received them no differently than when he was leading the assembly.
His character was noble, ancient, simple, and frugal; he did not engage in frivolous conversation. As he was about to enter parinirvāṇa, he asked his attendant, "Who is it?"
I built a seamless stupa. His attendant asked for the master’s design for the stupa, to which the master replied, "Even with all my strength, I cannot draw it.
He then passed away peacefully. After his cremation, his disciples collected the relics and remains and buried them to the left of Ying’an’s stupa.
He was eighty-four years old and had been a monk for sixty-eight years.
Master Yun’an Puyan of Daofang Monastery in Huzhou ascended the hall and said:
“I cite the occasion when Dongshan, while eating fruit on a winter night, asked Chief Seat Tai: ‘There is a thing that reaches up to heaven and down to earth; it is as black as lacquer;
it is ever present within activity, yet it cannot be contained within activity. Tell me, where does its fault lie? Tai replied: ‘Its fault lies in...’”
During a formal assembly, Mount (Dongshan) said, "Attendant, remove the fruit table. The Master (Caoshan) offered this verse:
"Dongshan brings disgrace to his family tradition; The Head Seat buries his own self. Pair upon pair of embroidered mandarin ducks— For a thousand ages they remain supported, yet cannot be raised.
In praise of the portrait of Venerable Zhaozhou, he said: "Pointlessly he brought up the seven-pound robe; How many practitioners have applied their minds to it?"
Everyone makes their nest in Qingzhou; they do not know that spring’s colors lie in Jiangnan.
Chan Master Shankaikai of Jinnshan Temple in Zhenjiang ascended the hall and said:
Master Miyuan once responded to Yinyuan’s question, "What is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? by saying, "A broken sand pot. The Master offered this verse: The Dharma Eye...
To bring it forth is already self-deception; for no reason, one mistakenly strikes the broken sand-pot. Now, throughout the entire world, it is difficult to conceal;
this calamity harms the monastic groves and brings trouble upon descendants.
Master Jue Tong of Huazang ascended the hall on the occasion of the Green Sprout Festival: "Shatter a single mote of dust and the Great Sutra emerges;
the soaring hawks and leaping fish become even more distinct. To not look with the eyes but to look with the mind is already to strike fire within ice once again.
Soaking black beans, one’s whole life is obscured; one must speak of the bountiful harvest beyond the kalpas. Spun into white snow, it rides upon the wind."
Layered greens; the yellow clouds of grain have been harvested, and the rice is now a vibrant green.

Master Chan Master Hiliàn of Shìyán on Jìngxīn Island in Wēnzhōu, a native of the Mǎ family from Cháoyáng, ascended the hall and cited the public case concerning the late-night conversation between Chan Master Guǎnghuì Lian and Prime Minister Yang Yi. The Master said: "The Secretary of State leans upon the Southern Dipper..."
The North Star: With vast wisdom, he turns the celestial pivot and reverses the terrestrial axis. Vast and empty for a thousand ages—who knows him?
A broken string must be mended with *luangjiao* glue. In the hall, a monk asked:

"In the past, when Zen Master Foguang of Fozhao was questioned by Emperor Xiaozong as to what Śākyamuni Buddha accomplished during his six years in the mountains, Fozhao replied: 'I thought Your Majesty had forgotten.'"
[The student] withdrew. What was the meaning of this? The Master answered with a verse: Great root, great vessel, great cultivation;
In a flash, the pivot turns toward the source. For ten billion years there has been but one Buddha; The Snowy Mountains have never separated the Dragon Palace.
Master Guangmu of Shaoshi at Ruiyan in Taizhou ascended the hall and said: He cited the case of Caoshan Xuanjue when a monk was standing in attendance.
Caoshan said, "The Way-farer, it is quite hot. The monk said, "Yes. Caoshan said, "As for this heat, where would you go to avoid it?
The monk said, "I would go into the cauldrons and the furnace embers to avoid it. Caoshan said, "But as for being inside the cauldrons and the furnace embers..."
"How do you avoid it? He replied, "The manifold sufferings cannot reach him. The Master then offered this verse:

"Blinding the three eyes at the crown of the head, One wanders freely amidst boiling cauldrons and glowing coals. If one says the manifold sufferings cannot reach him, Exactly where could they ever find a place to land?"
Master Wuxin of Beihai at Daochang Monastery in Huzhou cited the case of Huangbo when he was in the hall of Yanguan bowing to the Buddha.

At that time, Emperor Xuanzong of the Tang dynasty was a novice monk (śrāmaṇera) and asked: "If one does not seek the Buddha, does not seek the Dharma, and does not seek the Sangha, for what purpose do you prostrate?
Huangbo replied: "I always prostrate to such a reality. The novice monk asked: "What is the use of prostrating?"
When Yaowu struck him with his palm, the Master composed this verse: "Once he bestowed three palms upon the Sovereign; In the Buddha-dharma, what inch of growth has he ever had?
A coarse-practicing śramaṇa, sealed at the ultimate limit; To this day, there is no ground for shame."
Master Xuedou Wuxiang Fan of Siming ascended the hall and said: He cited Master Zhaozhou, who said, "As soon as there is right and wrong, confusion arises and the mind is lost.
Is there even any room for an answer? A monk recounted this to Luopu, who clicked his teeth together.
The monk then recounted it to Yunju, who said, "Why bother? When the monk returned and recounted it to Zhaozhou, Zhaozhou said, "The South..."
Many people have lost their bodies and forfeited their lives. The monk said, "I beg the Master to provide an illustration.

Zhaozhou was just about to repeat the previous story when the monk pointed to a monk nearby and said, "This monk has finished his meal; why does he speak such words? The Master composed a verse, saying:
Those sitting see those standing; those standing see those sitting. Alas, old Zhaozhou! In broad daylight, his eyes see ghosts.
Chan Master Yunchao Yan of Ruiyan in Taizhou composed a verse on copying scriptures, which says: "The character is not formed, yet the eight strokes are not wrong.
Held up in the open light, everyone knows it. Old Śākyamuni’s tongue has no bone; He took yellow leaves and..."
To frighten small children. A verse on the story of Lingyun seeing peach blossoms says: "March peach blossoms are in full, riotous red; Lingyun has lost his master and lord.
The old man Xuansha follows the deviant and pursues evil; Half is true feeling, half is empty deception."
Master Xuedou Dayie Qian of Siming ascended the hall and, citing Migan’s response to Yinyuan’s question, “What is the treasury of the true Dharma-eye?
Migan replied, “A broken sandpot. The Master composed a verse: “White jade carved into a bullet;
Gold cast into an iron Kunlun. This thousand-year-old滞貨 (stale wares) has no one to buy it; It cannot help but remain as such.”
Now, entrusting this to my descendants, he offered this verse for the monks: "Henghua once beat Kebin; The story remains a topic of conversation in the monasteries for a thousand years.
Let the yellow clouds and the staff be set aside for now; Simply brew some tea and see him out the door."
Chan Master Guyuan Dao of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou cited the case of Chan Master Danxia Ruian’s study under National Teacher Shitou.
One day, Shitou addressed the assembly, saying: "Tomorrow, mow the grass in front of the Buddha Hall. The Master composed a verse on this: Shitou mows the grass to test the heroic;
Dongmeng Danxia’s eyes were not high. Had he known how to turn his body and walk the living path, To this day...
"You should not burden your children.
Chan Master Jili Tanzhi of Tiger Hill in Suzhou first resided at Yanqing in Siming.
He subsequently moved to Qionglung in Su, Pujie in Zhenze, Ganlu in Zhenzhou, and Changlu. Upon arriving at Tiger Hill, he ascended the hall and, citing a monk—
A monk asked Xianglin, "What is the matter beneath the patched robe? Lin said, "In the twelfth month, fire burns the mountains.
The Master [Yanyue] said, "How has the rabbit ever been able to leave its burrow? If someone were to ask Yanqing, 'What is the matter beneath the patched robe?
I would simply answer him: 'The fish bought on the boat is especially delicious; the wine purchased after treading through the snow is doubly fragrant. He then ascended the hall and recited:

Reflect on the appearance of Śākyamuni in the world and the occasional descent of Maitreya; these are instances of suddenly transcending the state before heaven and earth were divided—how could they occur after heaven and earth have already been divided?
Without traversing the rungs of a ladder, one overturns the precious abode and departs in this very manner.
In this way, one can open immeasurable Dharma gates and expound hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings. (Suddenly grasping his staff, he strikes it once.)
He said: "The immeasurable Dharma gates and hundreds of thousands of wondrous meanings have all been ground to pieces right here.
Do you know where Tiger Hill has landed? Leaning on his staff, he said: 'The patriarch’s unfinished business brings calamity upon his descendants.
He then offered a verse on Lingyun’s talk of peach blossoms: "Peach blossoms bloom everywhere in the third month; Lingyun’s two eyes are filled with dust. Thank you, Master Xie!"
Reorganizing the hands that once fished for the giant turtle, one cannot avoid burying oneself in a single place.
Master Zhuo’an Zhao’s verse in praise of the Second Patriarch says: Seeking the mind, there is nowhere to find it; he deceived himself in vain.
He willingly endured the freezing cold of snow reaching his waist. Rising after three prostrations, he stood in his original position. Who would have known that the entire world is a surging wave?
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Wòlóng Pò’ān Xiān:
Chan Master Wúzhǔn Shífàn of Jìngshān, Hangzhou. Born in Zǐtóng, Shǔ, into the Yōng clan, he entered the monastic order at the age of nine under Dàoqīn of Yīnpíng Mountain.
Having mastered the classics and scriptures upon merely glancing at them, he ascended [the Dharma hall] in the fifth year of the Shàoxī era.
Having received full ordination, he traveled to Chengdu to observe the summer retreat under Zhengfa. There was an elder named Yao, a senior seat-holder and a high disciple of Xiatang;
the Master requested instruction from him on the method of sitting meditation. Yao asked, "What is this 'Chan' that you seek to sit? Who is it that sits?

The Master took these words to heart and investigated them day and night. One day, while at the toilet, he attained realization regarding this dialogue. He then took his leave and went to rely upon Fozhao.
At the East Hermitage of Emperor Ying’s Monastery, Zhao asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "I am from Jianzhou. Zhao asked, "Did you bring your sword with you?
As soon as these words were spoken, the Master let out a shout. Zhao laughed and said, "This black-headed fellow is acting recklessly.

Because he was extremely poor and lacked the funds for a tonsure, people referred to him by the nickname "Black-Headed One" (Wutouzi). Not long after, he heard that Pōān was residing at Xiling in Suzhou.
Huaxiu Peak went to visit him. A man named Chundian entered the room next; his faculties were sharp and he showed no deference.
Master An struck him until they reached the Dharma Hall, intending to expel him. The Master (Huaxiu) mediated, saying, "It is but a common occurrence for Chan practitioners to contend over Chan;
why stop at this? Master An said, "Have you not heard it said: 'When my stomach is hungry, hearing the sound of the board, I go to eat rice'?"
Upon hearing these words, the Master involuntarily broke into a cold sweat that drenched his back. Later, when he served as the First Seat at Lingyin under Pò’ān, he went once more to follow him.
While attending Pò’ān during a visit to Shíshǔn Ān, a practitioner of the monastery requested instruction, saying, "The monkey cannot be caught;
I beg the Master for an expedient means. Pò’ān replied, "What is the use of trying to catch it? It is like wind blowing across water."
A natural pattern formed [on his robe]. As the Master stood by his side, the burden that had long weighed upon his heart was suddenly released.
He lived as a hermit in a cloud-nest on Mount Qionglong in Wu County. Later, he moved to Ruiwang Temple and then to Ruiyan in Taizhou.

When the Abbot Zhi invited the Master to share the teaching seat, the Master was at Ruiyan when he suddenly dreamed of a person in magnificent robes and cap who presented him with a handful of thatch grass. The following day, a special messenger arrived from Qingliang in Mingzhou.
Upon his arrival, when he entered the monastery, he saw that the deity of the temple was surnamed Mao; his attire and physical appearance were no different from those seen in his previous dream.
Subsequently, he moved to Mount Jiaoshan and then to Xuedou. He was successively commanded by imperial decree to move to Yuwang and then to Jing Mountain.

The Master resided at Jing Mountain for twenty years; his stores were abundant and his assembly was as vast as the sea. Although it suffered the calamity of fire during the Bingding year, it was soon restored to its former state.

In his observation, he saw that the Dharma assembly was at its peak. A monk asked, "Zhaozhou said, 'Thirty years ago, at the head of the brazier, there was a story about having neither guest nor host.
No one has ever brought this up before. What is the meaning of this? The Master replied, "His tongue drags across the ground."
The monk asked, "Ultimately, what is the 'guestless and hostless' dialogue? The Master said, "Words fill the world.
The monk asked, "As for Xuefeng hearing this and saying, 'This old fellow’s heels have not even touched the ground,' how do you explain that? The Master said, "Bury them all in one pit.
The monk said, "It can truly be called striking the ice through to the bottom with a scorched brick; it is like a blind man bumping into [the truth]."
"Matchhead. The Master said, "A single stroke cuts it off. Ascending the hall, he said: "At Vulture Peak they pointed to the moon; at Caoxi they spoke of the moon.
Passed down from generation to generation, they have taken a tortoise and turned it into a turtle. Elder Fan usually has a mouth hanging on the wall that has never been used.
Today, for no reason, he has entered this profession. When matters come to this, one can do nothing but shake things up from the east."

Xibo said, "I cannot help but take up this many-year almanac and point out some of its errors and deceptions for you all to see, so that Guo Da, Li Er, Deng Si, and Zhang San may know that it is cold in spring and hot in autumn throughout Jiangnan and the Two Zhe regions.
Although this is so, the Yellow River clears only once every three thousand years. He ascended the hall and said, "If we were to discuss this matter..."
This matter is simply straightforward, concise, and easy to understand; it is mostly people who create difficulties for themselves and erect obstacles for themselves.
Thus, sometimes when I see people on the eastern or western corridors bowing in greeting, I simply lower my head to receive them.
In truth, there is nothing else to it: I only wish for everyone to recognize that this old man is from Longqing Prefecture in Xichuan.
Regarding human affairs: if you can recognize them, then you may engage in some local dialects and tell some local stories with everyone else.
For now, let us not speak of whether you have recognized the Elder; rather, each of you should at least know your own native place.
Do you know it? Mingzhou has six counties; Fenghua has eight districts. Entering the hall: Under the Five Peaks, there is nothing at all.
The monks' beds are cramped and the offerings in the hall are sparse. Underfoot are broken bricks and shattered shards;
before one’s eyes are encountered Wang the Wild Man and Li the Madman. To dwell on this mountain with such meager merit is truly to betray the Old Barbarian.
Nevertheless, let it be made even clearer. Entering the hall: One summer has already passed; there is nothing that has not been settled.
Suifú possessed a *pātra* (alms bowl), and Gōngzhōu possessed a porcelain bowl. Emperor Lǐzōng once summoned him to the Xiūzhèng Hall;

his responses were detailed and lucid, moving the Emperor to a change of countenance. The Emperor bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered *saṃghāṭī* robe and further decreed that he ascend the seat at Címíng Hall.
The Emperor drew back his curtain to listen. He presented the essential teachings spoken by the Master to Chen Gong Guiyi, the Senior Censor.

Chen Gong memorialized the throne, stating that these were concise, direct, and beneficial to the sacred governance. Consequently, the Master was bestowed with the title Chan Master Fojian, along with gifts of silk, cloth, gold, silver, and other items.
Forty *li* from the monastery, the Master built a hermitage to receive wandering monks. Emperor Lizong personally sprinkled [ink]...

The Imperial Calligraphy bestowed upon him as a temple plaque read: "Ten Thousand Years of Continuity. On the first day of the third month in the Jihou year of Chunyou (1249), he addressed the assembly, saying:
"This mountain monk is both old and ill; I lack the strength to engage in idle chatter with you all here and there.
Today, I have forced myself out to shake off, before you all, everything that I have failed to express in my previous teachings."
He then rose from his seat, shook out his robes, and asked, "How much is this? On the fifteenth day, he personally wrote his final memorial and several dozen letters;
his speech and laughter were as light and humorous as they had been during his ordinary days. While a physician was examining his pulse, the Master said to him, "You do not yet recognize this pulse.
At dawn on the eighteenth day, he requested a brush and wrote a verse: "When coming, it was empty and desolate; when departing, it is likewise."
Naked as a strip of red silk, he sought further to inquire into the ultimate point. At Tiantai there was a stone bridge; having crossed it in a mere moment, he passed away.
His entire body was interred beside Zhengxu, and his stupa was named Yuanzhao.
Chan Master Shitian Faxun of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was born into the Peng family of Meishan. From birth, he possessed keen intelligence.
He left the household life under Zhiming of Fabao Monastery on Mount Shilong in Danling. While traveling, he reached Shichuang to pay homage at the stupa of Leqian, where he composed a verse, saying:
"A single thought of compassionate countenance is fundamentally never separated; why need one suddenly display such eccentricity? Leveling the high..."
His compassionate heart was so earnest that it distressed Lei Gong (the Thunder God), who kept him busy all night long. Because of this, the Master’s fame grew greatly.

When he heard that Pō’ān’s reputation for the Way was flourishing at Qiónglóng in Wúmén, he went there to rely upon him. In the meditation hall, when the master raised the case of the World-Honored One holding up a flower and Kāśyapa smiling, the Master said:
"A scorched brick strikes the frozen ground to its very core; red-eyed, one bumps into a firebrand."

An-yin marveled at this; as he constantly observed the Master’s conduct in daily life—whether speaking or remaining silent—his doubts were aroused. The Master thereupon resolved to seek refuge under him.
Together with Wu-zhun, they exhorted and sharpened one another every day. After a long time, the Master emerged into the world at Gao-feng in Su-chou, and subsequently moved to Pu-ming at Feng-qiao.
Among his contemporaries, Gao-yuan Quan, Wu-xiang Fan, Ji-an Jue, and Shi-xi Yue all relied upon him for guidance.

While he was residing there, the Zhongshan Monastery left its seat vacant, and the Master was appointed to fill it. At the beginning of the Baoding era, an imperial decree summoned him to Jingci Monastery;
in the second year of the Duanping era, another decree summoned him to Lingyin Monastery. Ascending the hall, he said: "One path is direct; two paths are circuitous.

If a monk understands this, he perceives ten thousand distinctions and a thousand differences. With eyes leisurely cast across the courtyard, spring has ended yet flowers still remain. The old barbarian [Bodhidharma] ought not to have crossed the flowing sands."
Ascending the hall: The substance of the Great Way is vast; it is neither easy nor difficult. Buying a hat by measuring the head—this land and the Western Heaven.

Ascending the hall: To recognize the mind is for mountains and peaks to sink away. Grasping gold turns it to earth; grasping earth turns it to gold. Behind the feet and before the feet, it is ready-made merchandise.
Yet before the Peak of Shaoshi, one cannot pass the point of intersection. Ascending the hall: There is jade within the stone, but no oil in the sand.

Before Deshan and Linji emerged from the common stream, I instead recall Cold Mountain (Han Shan). At times he stood at an ancient ferry crossing. Entering the hall, [he said]: "Seeing, hearing, sensing, and knowing;
walking, standing, sitting, and lying down—these have already been missed by being cast above the eyebrows. Barefoot, singing a mountain song, there is no one on the road to join him.
Entering the hall, [he said]: "He locks fast the heavy barrier; the lives of all you people are in the hands of this mountain monk."
[The Master] turns [the robe] inside out. He lets loose a single thread. "The life of this mountain monk rests in the hands of you all.
Now, I neither hold fast nor let loose. This mountain monk is you; you are this mountain monk.
After thirty years, do not say that Jiangshan has been mixing mud with water. Entering the hall: Since the time of chaos, thirty years have passed without a moment’s decrease.
Salt and sauce. Master Mazu left things in a state of total disorder; Ling Shan was not like that. Since the time of confusion began, thirty years have passed without it diminishing.
After a long silence, he said, "It is difficult to deceive those who wear the patched robes. He spoke this verse for the assembly: "To turn one's body upon a sword's edge is still dull;
To ask for directions at one's own doorstep is most senseless. A chicken of Chu is no phoenix from the Vermilion Mountains; Why must one face the wind?"

He groomed his feathers and wings. On the full moon day of the third month in the year Jiachen of the Chunyou era, he addressed his disciples, saying: "If you only obtain the root, do not worry about the branches.
What do you call the root? What do you call the branches? A pine or cypress remains green for a thousand years, yet it does not accord with the tastes of the people of this age."

"The peony blooms red for a single day; the young gentlemen of the entire city are intoxicated. When the mountain monk spoke thus, he said, "If there is anyone who does not agree with this, they are my fellow student.
Disciple Shi Jun painted a portrait of the Master and requested a eulogy, in which it was written:
"The final phrase is entrusted to Chushan. Many were quite surprised by this. Previously, the Master had established a reception hall at Xixi called Baoshou.
Suddenly manifesting an illness, he retired to Baoshou Monastery to prepare for his end. He instructed that his entire body be interred on the mountain behind the monastery.
Sitting upright, he passed away. He was seventy-five years of age and fifty-three years since his ordination.
Master Cijue of Yunju in Jiangzhou ascended the hall and said: “I cite the case where King Min asked Xuefeng, ‘What if I wish to build a Buddhist hall?
What do you think? Xuefeng replied, ‘Great King, why not build a Hall of the Empty King instead?
The King said, ‘Please show me the master’s model. Xuefeng extended both hands. Yunmen said, ‘One move accomplishes four things.’”
Nineteen. The Master’s verse says: The model for the Hall of the Empty King; Xuefeng spreads his two hands wide. Adding to this, Old Shaoyang Delivers forty-nine blows at once.
All of them are facing south to gaze at the Big Dipper. A verse in praise of the Venerable Shipman:
For over thirty years at Yaoshan, How could he transmit the livelihood of ghosts? Had it not been for Old Jia Shan at that time, [The teaching would have perished.]
"Be patient for now and endure until the boat is broken through.
Chan Master Duan'an Daocou of Daci Monastery in Siming offered this verse to a cobbler: "The work of reaching the bottom has already been perfected;
One must know that the secret place is transmitted from one's own mind. The heels of the feet touch the ground and follow its turn; Treading upon it..."
He has not donned [the monastic robes] even in a donkey’s year.
[The lineage of] Chan Master Caoyuan Sheng of Guifeng.
○ Chan Master Chijue Daochong of Jing Mountain in Hangzhou, son of the Gou family of Changjiang, Wuxin; his mother was surnamed Guo.

He was born with broad shoulders and a short stature; his natural disposition far surpassed that of others. From his youth until adulthood, he studied for the jinshi examination while simultaneously pursuing the teachings of the Śākya clan.
At Miaoyin Monastery in Zizhou, he received the tonsure from Master Xiuzheng. He traveled to Chengdu to study the sūtras and śāstras at Shengci Monastery;
however, becoming weary of the scholastic analysis of names and characteristics (*nāma-lakṣaṇa*), he abandoned them once more. Hearing that Songyuan was proclaiming the Way in Raozhou...
He went directly to the gate of Jianfu Monastery, but because of the famine that year, he was not admitted. Cao Yuan, serving as the head seat at Yunju, later took up the abbacy at Miaoguo;

when the Master entered his hall, he attained realization upon hearing Yuan’s introductory words. Yuan subsequently appointed him to attend to the incense, yet he did not spare him the "old fist" or the painful staff, never relenting.
At this point, the Master’s lifelong views and knowledge vanished entirely, leaving not even a trace behind. When Yuan moved to Guifeng, the Master again attended him there.
After traveling for some time, he presented a verse to take his leave, saying: "I still have these two hands of a destitute man; I shall go to scratch the itchy places throughout all quarters.
This became widely circulated throughout the Jianghu region. When he arrived in Hangzhou, Songyuan was presiding at Lingyin Monastery; its gates were strict and its doors formidable.
For eight months he was not permitted to enter the inner quarters. Some reported that the Master had been lost; Yuan said, "I have already opened the gates wide for him to stay;
it is simply that he has missed his opportunity face-to-face. When the Master heard these words, he saw through them completely. He served Cao Yuan at Miaoguo and Guipeng;
at that time, whether laughing, joking, scolding, or reviling, everything was a skillful means for the benefit of others. Jia-ding Ji (1209).
In the Year of the Rabbit, he succeeded to the abbacy at Jiashuo Guangxiao as the First Seat of Mount Jing;

his reputation for the Way reached the imperial court, and the Prince of Wei, the Minister of Education Shi [Kai], appointed him to Jiangshan by official decree. Later, when Minister Cao Bin governed Fujian, he invited him to Mount Gu.

He had not yet set out when Xuefeng’s summons arrived. Having served for half a year, the imperial decree for Tiantong was issued; the assembly gathered like the sea, as during the height of Hongzhi’s time.
As the seat at Yuyang remained vacant, he assumed the duties of abbot, traveling between the two mountains to preach the Dharma.
In the Jiachen year of the Chunyou era, an imperial edict transferred him to Lingyin. The Master said, "My grandfather, Mian, and my uncle, Songyuan, propagated the Way."
This was his native land. He was just about to exert himself with vigor to revive the ancestral tradition when worldly circumstances arose that did not satisfy his aspirations.
He beat the drum to bid farewell to the assembly and retired in seclusion to Jinling. The Imperial Court appointed him to Huqiu to allow him to enjoy his old age, but he did not accept.
When Lord Xu Zhai, the Regional Commander-in-Chief, invited him from Jiangshan, he likewise declined. Later, when Xiweng of Yuyang resigned from his post, the court deliberated that—

Upon learning of this, he went to his home and summoned the Master to his secluded retreat. The messenger returned three times, yet the Master ultimately did not respond to the summons. The following year, Lord Zhao, the Governor of the Capital, invited him to open the mountain at Fahuaseng.
As the Master was about to take charge of the affairs at Mount Jing, the imperial decree arrived; the Master wished to decline the Fahuaseng invitation along with it.

He reasoned that if he did not go to Fahuaseng, he would fail in his word, whereas if he seriously disobeyed the sovereign’s command, it would be a lack of reverence. To lose both [his promise and his reverence]—[he could not bear it].
Xin took this as a lesson for his later studies and suddenly changed his course. He stayed at Fahua for over a month, then immediately ascended Mount Jing.

Both humans and spirits responded in harmony, and the sound of joyful acclaim was like thunder. Entering the hall, a monk asked: "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings—these three are without distinction.
What is the past mind? The Master said: "Set it aside and wait until it has cooled, then come look. The monk said: "If..."
"What is the present mind? The Master said, "I shall answer you as you ask. The monk asked, "What is the future mind?
The Master said, "I will tell you when I ascend the hall next time. The monk asked, "What is the past Buddha? The Master said, "Last year’s plum blossoms.
The monk asked, "What is the present Buddha? The Master said, "This year’s willows. The monk asked, "What is the [future] Buddha? The Master said, "..."
[The monk] asked about the Buddha of the future. The Master said, "His countenance and fragrance remain as they were.

The monk asked, "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the past? The Master struck the left side of the meditation seat with his whisk. The monk asked, "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the present?

The Master struck the right side of the meditation seat with his whisk. The monk asked, "What is the wisdom of differentiation regarding the future? The Master [struck the center of the meditation seat with his whisk].
He placed a single dot in the middle of his whisk. The monk said, "Mind, Buddha, and sentient beings have no turning away from one another;
the ocean of lands in the ten directions is contained within a single hair. He then prostrated. The Master then said, "The past mind cannot be apprehended;
the present mind cannot be apprehended; the future mind cannot be apprehended. Since the three periods of time cannot be apprehended, what do you call 'discriminating wisdom'?"

If a person attains thorough penetration, they will see that the Buddhas of the three periods of time have never for a single moment failed to turn the Great Dharma Wheel atop the crowns of everyone’s heads.
What more is there to seek here by jostling shoulders and standing toe-to-toe? [The Master] drives them all away at once with his staff.

Ascending the hall for the summer retreat: In the monastery of Perfect Enlightenment (*Pūrṇabodhi*), every dust mote has its own path; sitting and cutting off coming and going, one is suddenly enlightened.
Empty throughout past and present. Thirteen there, fifteen here; before and after, not differing by so much as a hair’s breadth.

It is laughable that the Yellow-Faced Gautama, even to this day, does not know where he has fallen. Entering the hall, [the Master said]: "The entire universe and great earth do not occupy so much as a single thread or hair’s breadth.
This is the path upon which you all carry your staffs across your shoulders and travel on pilgrimage throughout the four worlds. I have no place [for them]."
"Not yet. There is nothing he does not know. But tell me, what Dharma did the Master Śīlabhadra at Nālandā Monastery in India preach today?

Having said this, he descended from his seat. He then ascended the hall and said: "There is one person who, through a single moment of thought, suddenly realizes [enlightenment] and falls among the ranks of the Buddhas."
There was once a man who, throughout kalpas of rebirth, remained an icchantika and had no wish to attain Buddhahood. Tell me, which one is fit to receive the offerings of devas and humans?
After a long silence, he said: "A butterfly pierces the fragrant path, its two brows damp; a bee robs the withered flower, its two thighs stout.

When approaching his passing, he wrote by hand a record for his reliquary stupa and several dozen letters of farewell, saying: "The anniversary of Wuzu’s death falls on the eighteenth day of the third month."
On the day of the fifteenth, I was about to depart and could not offer incense or prepare an offering. The attendant monk urgently requested a farewell verse.
The Master said to him, "The final word cannot be deliberated upon; it requires that each person directly take it up for themselves."
He immediately took up his brush to write. He bid farewell to the assembly and ascended the hall; as he spoke, it was past midnight, and he rose from his seat. After a short while, he passed away.
He was eighty-two years of age and had been a monk for sixty-one years. His body was cremated, and the relics were of five colors in countless numbers.

His disciples followed his final instructions and escorted his remains back to be interred at Jinling. The scholars at Yushan Hermitage, unable to bear their longing and grief, requested that Hanzhong divide half of them for them.
The stupa was built at Yuzhi Hermitage in Changpu Field.
[This is the record of] Chan Master Jichuang Youzhao of Yewang in Siming, a successor of Chan Master Kuzhen Jing of Tiantong. He was of the Deng clan of Fuzhou, Min County, and relied upon Jiufeng.
Huidé of Róngān received the tonsure. At that time, Kúcán was propagating the Way at Yishān, so he went there to follow him. One day, Kúcán said:
"Since the very first sight of the peach blossoms, until now, I have had no further doubts. "Where," [Huidé] asked, "is it that he has no doubts?"
The Master laughed heartily and hurried out. Chanshen approved of him. When Chanshen moved to Lingyin, the Master served as the internal recorder (*neiji*).
Subsequently, he was held in high esteem by Damei Shiyuan, Huqiu Jili, Maofeng Wuzhun, Jinshan Daxie, and others, all of whom regarded him with great respect.
Because his mother was elderly, he returned home to visit her at Xuefeng. Chijue retained him as the head of the secretarial office (*jishi*).
Zhao Gong Ruyou, the Military Governor of Min, admired the Master’s reputation and commissioned him to propagate the Dharma at Dongshan Dacheng and to reside at Huangbo in Fuzhou.

At that time, Lin Gong Xiyi, the Left Historian of Zhuxi, followed the Master to discuss the heart-dharma, serving him with sincere devotion. Zhuxi composed a poem which says: "In my old age, I have obtained..."

My friends were like teachers and elders; when they departed one by one, who was there to accompany me? By imperial decree, I was appointed to the heart of the river, and by edict, I was transferred to Yujia.
Just as a disaster struck, I exerted all my strength to rebuild the various halls. When they were somewhat complete, I went to pay my respects to the Chancellor, Lord Jia Wei-gong.
Upon hearing my report, the court granted gold and silk to construct a precious *śarīra* stūpa, thereby restoring the former regulations in their entirety. A monk asked: "What is the Buddha?"
The Master said, "The Eight Auspicious Ones. The monk asked, "What is the Dharma? The Master said, "The Six Excellences.
The monk asked, "What is the Sangha? The Master said, "Its face and eyes are present right now. He ascended the hall and said: "The six sense objects are not evil;

they are identical to perfect enlightenment. Crows caw 'ka-ka,' magpies chirp 'chao-chao. North of the river and south of the river, the tides rise and fall. In the second month of spring, the flowers and grasses [bloom]."
Fragrance. Where does Sudhana seek the pavilion? Ha! Entering the hall: What is the Way? A wooden post.
What is Chan? A brick. When the ancient worthies gave such instructions, ten out of twenty remained complacent and took no account of them;
they did not realize that [the Master] was precisely scratching the itchy spot on Mount Mao. Why? Because when building a temple, it is exactly what is needed.
Master Qingxi Yuan of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou ascended the hall and said: "When Bodhidharma came from the West, he occupied the entire ground of one sitting mat.
After Shenkang paid him three prostrations, it was all claimed at once. This has caused the descendants of later generations to each divide up the boundaries and establish their own domains.
Zen monks today pull through the grass and gaze into the wind, traveling from Wu in the morning to Yue in the evening; they range from South Heaven Peak in the north to Mount Wutai in the south."
The Platform. Has the tip of the staff or the sole of the sandal ever been stepped upon? After a long silence: "Above all, do not step upon it!
Chan Master Yugou Zhi of Fashi Temple in Quanzhou spoke in verse of his mountain dwelling:

"A saffron robe of a thousand or ten hundred patches, Leaning against a pine, I rub my belly and watch the clouds fly. If someone asks me about the wonder of the clouded mountains, I tell them: 'In the depths of spring, the bamboo shoots.'"
Bracken Fertility.
○ Chan Master Yuetam Yuan of Xichan Monastery in Fuzhou ascends the hall for the opening of the furnace: "Everyone guards the sky within the jar;
though earth overturns and heaven turns, I am not thus. With a single blow of the hammer, sparks fly forth; the Luo River is burned away, and I thank [the ancestors]."
Langchuan praised Master Zhoutou, saying: "Bloody and raw—this is the heart-mind of the ancient Buddha. How many times has it been raised?
Who is the one who knows it?
Baen Taigu Xian Chanshi ascended the hall and said: "If one discusses this matter, it does not involve thought, mind, intention, or conception."

It is not a matter of dry silence, silent illumination, or forgetting the self; one must attain a state of transparent clarity. To do so, one must undergo a "sweat" [a moment of intense breakthrough].

After the sweat has broken out, what then? He calls his attendant and says, "Bring me my fan. Ascending the hall, he says: "The night is cold and the frost heavy; the wind blows and the chill increases further.
As the seasons pass by in negligence, how is it with your own fundamental matter? He strikes the meditation seat and says: "It is not something known through intellectual understanding."

Regarding this sound, how can it be pointed out to others? Entering the hall, [the Master said: "In the life of a patch-robed monk traveling on pilgrimage, parting the weeds and observing the wind, the first requirement is to recognize the path;
only then will you succeed. When the path is not mistaken, east, west, south, and north everywhere become one's home."
There is a slight detour; at five li there is a single signpost, and at ten li there are twin markers. Where is it? Even further than that!
[The Master] throws down his staff and says, "Look beneath your feet!"
Master Xixi Xi of Gong’an, Jingnan Prefecture, ascended the hall and said: "The place where mind-mind is shallow is in truth most profound;
the Way that is remote and obscure has no one who reaches it. If you walk too fast, you will not tread upon it; if you walk too slow, you will miss it.
For many springs the flowers have bloomed while Shaolin sat in meditation; yet I still recall the Western-come Bodhidharma."
The Verse on the Buddha’s Birthday by Chan Master Chun Weng Jie says: The poisonous seeds of Vairambha wind have blossomed into toxic flowers, Adding to Yunmen’s cup after his drunken bout.
Today at Keqiao, the weather turns foul; Thin mist and sparse rain wash away the yellow plum blossoms. (Note:
This verse is recorded in the *Zadudhai* as being composed by Xiyuan, but that is an error.)
Master Gaofeng Chong’s verse on the story of the First Patriarch meeting Emperor Wu of the Liang dynasty: Unfurling his banners and deploying his array, he entered the realm of Liang;

Before even beholding the Emperor’s countenance, he had already surrendered. Though he possessed supernatural powers, they could not be displayed; With a single reed boat, he floated lightly across the Long River.
The Dharma Successor of Chan Master Yanjing Wan’an Rou:
○ Chan Master Shuangshan Yuan of Tiger Hill, Suzhou, Ascends the Hall. He cites the case where Master Miyun Yuanwu was asked by Master Ying’an:
“What is the Treasury of the True Dharma Eye? Miyun replied: “A broken sand-pot. The Master offers this verse: The Lords of the Five Tombs...
When I was a youth, I delighted in the spring breeze as my horse’s hooves leaped along. I spared no golden coins for pellets, striking the yellow orioles beneath the *haitang* blossoms.
On the walls of the two corridors at Cold Spring, he inscribed a verse that said: "In every single atom, there is a firm and dense body."
Changing one's head and face, transforming the spirit—who would have known that striking the east wall hits the west wall? All are people from the assembly on Vulture Peak.
This is the lineage of Chan Master Wuguang of Yuyuan.
Chan Master Fozhi Huiji Yuanxi of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was of the Tang clan of Yuzhang, whose family had been engaged in the study of Confucianism for generations.
Master Ming of Mount Xishan’s Mingjue Monastery was the master’s paternal uncle; he gathered the younger members of the clan to instruct them in the secular classics.
The Master and his elder brother, Yuanling, both studied for the jinshi examinations. Once Yuanling had passed the examinations, the Master subsequently followed Master Ming.

The Master shaved his head, intending to travel to various regions. His mother privately prepared silver to provide for his journey, but the Master said, "Wealth is sufficient to ruin one's resolve," and skillfully declined it.
He set out without carrying a single coin. Hearing that Wuchu was spreading the Dharma at Yujia, he went to rely upon him.
Wuchu was struck with wonder and amazement by their conversation and kept him in his service. Later, he visited Dongsou Ying at Nanping.

He ordered his secretary to record this. During the Zhizhi era of the Yuan dynasty, the Imperial Commissioner Yang Lianzhenjia was commissioned by imperial decree to procure the śarīra relics from Yuyang Monastery.
He personally visited the Master to request a record of the origins and details of the relics and invited him to accompany him. The Master declined, saying, "I have an elderly mother."

After the war, his fate became unknown; he subsequently returned to Jiangxi. At that time, Yuanling had already died while serving as the Vice Prefect of Linjiang under the Chancellor Zhang (Zhang Xiang), leaving only his mother at home.
Shifeng served her with such filial piety that it became renowned. In the second year of the Yuanzhen era, he took up the abbacy at Baizhang.
After twelve years, the Dharma seat flourished, and at the beginning of the Zhida era, he accepted the invitation to lead Jingci Temple.

He entered the monastery. Daily, he traveled to the Zhongshusheng and the Xuanzhengyuan, where the officials prostrated themselves to welcome him and request that he proclaim the essential tenets of the school.

Eminent monks from all quarters gathered like spokes converging on a hub. He ascended the hall and said: "Yunmen spoke the word 'Universal' (Pu), such that no one in the entire world can do anything about it.
Yet they fail to realize that Yunmen was planting his four corners firmly upon the ground. At that time, had he [the Master] instead let out a single roar of awe..."
He shouted, "Understood! This old man was provoked to anger; slowly, [Zhaozhou] offered a greeting and said, "Please do not take offense.

Not only did he help this old man up, but it is certain that his words would circulate throughout the world. He ascended the hall and cited the story of Upāsaka Fu of Taiyuan, who attained enlightenment upon hearing the sound of a horn.
He then offered this verse: Qinsheng entered the vast ocean; The Grand Historian traveled to famous mountains. From this point on, Yangzhou...

On the road outside the city, the regulations were strict and did not permit the gates to open early. He ascended the hall and said: "In the Three Realms there is no dharma; where can one seek the mind?
White clouds form a canopy, and flowing springs serve as a lute. Throughout antiquity and today there has been no interval— who is the one who knows this music? He struck his whisk and said:
"One song, two songs—no one understands them. After the rain, the night pond’s autumn waters run deep. Ascending the hall:

Sitting alone on the Great Hero Peak, Cold ashes cannot be stirred to red. A single spark of fire emerges; A solitary crane flies past Liaodong. [This was the discourse for the opening of the retreat.]
Making a gesture with his hands as if tying the mouth of a cloth bag, he said: "Today, Nanshan has finished tying the mouth of the cloth bag.
You all, each and every one, must dwell in the wisdom of equanimity within it, with body and mind at peace.

Should there suddenly be someone who breaks through the azure void and knocks down Mount Sumeru, do not say that the knot was not tied securely. After a long silence, he said: "The net that covers the heavens."
He resided there for seven years before moving to Mount Jing. Subsequently, he took up his staff and returned to the foot of Mount Nanping.

Hearing that the Master had retired, disciples from Baizhang and Dayang vied with one another to invite him; unable to refuse their requests, he eventually returned to Mount Yang, where he stayed for three years.
When he was about to pass away, he wrote letters by hand to those with whom he had corresponded, composed a verse for the assembly, and cast aside his brush, passing into extinction.
This was the seventeenth day of the intercalary eighth month in the sixth year of the Yanyou era. He was eighty-two years old.
He was buried beneath Jinji Stone. His disciples in Hangzhou also divided his fingernails and hair to enshrine them in stupas at Jingci and Xiyin.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Zangsou Zhen of Mount Jing:
Chan Master Yuansou Xingduan of Mount Jing, Hangzhou. He was of the He clan of Linhai, whose family had been Confucian scholars for generations.

His mother, Lady Chen, was able to master the Five Classics. When [Hui]si was six years old, his mother taught him the *Lunyu* (Analects) and the *Mengzi* (Mencius), and he was immediately able to recite them from memory.
At twelve, he received the tonsure under his paternal cousin, Master Maoshang, at Huacheng Monastery in Yuhang.
Upon receiving full ordination, he was naturally able to master all forms of written literature without relying on a teacher’s instruction. He dedicated his will to the Great Dharma. To this end—
He forgot both sleep and food. When he first attended Zang-sou at Mount Jing, Zang-sou asked, "Where are you from?
The Master replied, "Taizhou. Zang-sou gave a shout. The Master spread his sitting mat. Zang-sou shouted again. The Master withdrew his sitting mat.
Zang-sou said, "I grant you thirty blows; go attend the hall. At these words, the Master attained a sudden and great awakening. One day, while serving him, Zang-sou said, "I..."

"Quannan (Southern Spring) has no monks," [the Master] said. The Teacher replied, "What about the Abbot? The Old Man then struck him. The Teacher caught the staff and said, "Do not say there are no monks.

The Old Man nodded his approval and immediately invited him to serve in the office of the Attendant. After the Old Man passed away, he went to Jingci Temple to serve as the Secretary under Master Shilin Gong.
Subsequently, because the mountains and waters of Lingyin were exceptionally pure and magnificent, he went there to hang his staff. The Master once said of himself:
He was known as a native of Hanshi Village. Hengchuan, while at Yuwang Monastery, invited him with a verse that said:
"Throughout the vastness of heaven and earth, there is only Hanshanzi. However, the Master ultimately did not cross the river to visit Jue’an Zhen at Chengtian Monastery;
instead, he visited Xueyan Qin at Yangshan. Xueyan asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "From West Zhejiang. Xueyan asked, "For what reason..."
Their voices were different. The Master said, "Shut that stinking mouth! Yankuan said, "The otter path is high, the bridge is lofty, and the gathered clouds peak is steep;
I do not yet know where the record-keeper resides. The Master clapped his hands and said, "A duck swallows a snail; its eyes protrude!
Yankuan laughed, looked back at his attendant, and said, "Bring some fine tea. He then escorted the Master back to the Mengtang Hall. After three years, Yankuan passed away. Thereupon...
He returned to the region south of the Zhe River. While Fuhui was residing at Mount Jing, he invited the Master to serve as the First Seat.

Subsequently, the Master withdrew to the Lengqia Chamber, where he composed over a hundred poems modeled after those of Hanshan Zi; all were streams of the True Vehicle, which many monastics from all quarters transmitted and recited.
In the Gengzi year of the Dade era, he entered the world at Zifu Temple in Huzhou. His fame reached the capital, and by special imperial decree, he was granted [the title of Chan Master].
Chan Master Huiwen Zhengbian was first recommended by Zhang Lü, the Minister of the Secretariat and Acting Director of the Xuanzheng Yuan, to preside over Zhongzhu.
He subsequently moved to Lingyin Monastery. By imperial decree, he was summoned to the Jinshan Monastery to perform the Water and Land *śrāddha* feast and preach the Dharma.

Upon the completion of the ceremony, he entered the presence of the Emperor at the Private Audience Hall; his responses were in accord with the Imperial will, and he was further granted the title of Buddha.
He was bestowed with the title "The Sun That Shines Universally. Upon taking his leave of the Emperor and returning south, he retired to the West Hermitage at Liangzhu to cultivate his virtue.

In the year Renxu of the Zhizhi era, the seat of Mount Jingshan became vacant; the leaders of the three schools and the fourfold assembly collectively petitioned the Xuanzheng Yuan for the Master to fill the position.
Consequently, they submitted a joint memorial requesting an imperial edict to protect and support him. By this time, he had already received the golden-embroidered *kāṣāya* three times.
By his grace, for twenty years his feet did not cross the threshold of the gate. Those who admired his Way gathered like fish scales, so numerous that there was no room to contain them.

Even those who had long considered themselves masters of the Way would, upon his arrival, find their spirits withered and their resolve dissolved, wishing instead to take a place among the junior disciples.
A monk asked, "What is the treasury of the true Dharma-eye? The Master said, "The 'Stone Brave-at-Heart' at the crossroads. The monk said, "Is it not just this?"
"It is just so. The Master said, "The moon is like a drawn bow; there is little rain, but much wind.
He ascended the hall and, citing a monk who asked Zhaozhou, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature? Zhaozhou replied, "No. Then another monk asked, "Does a dog have Buddha-nature?
Zhaozhou replied, "Yes. The Master said, "If 'no' were the ultimate truth, why did he later say 'yes'?"
"If you take the conditioned as being true, why did he previously say it is non-existent? Here, having caught Zhaozhou in the act, I grant you the heights of heaven and earth.

Ascending the hall: "The autumn wind is cool; the autumn night is long. The traveler who has not yet returned thinks of his hometown. [He] strikes the meditation seat. "From this point on, one will not return;
once one returns, it is attained. Who can compete for the misty scenery of the Five Lakes? Ascending the hall: "The mind is not..."
"Buddha! Rabbits and horses have horns; wisdom is not the Way. Oxen and sheep have no horns. [The Master] suddenly picked up his staff, drew a line, and said:
"A night of falling flower rain; the whole city is filled with the fragrance of flowing water. The Master once examined a newly arrived monk, saying: "Where do you holy ones come from?
Where are your numinous spirits? The monk replied: "Lin-zhen-zhen. The Master said: "Fabricated Chan practitioners are as numerous as hemp seeds."
"It looks like millet. Go to the hall. He then examined another monk, saying, "The chessboard stone will split your forehead;

the bowl-basin pool will soak rotten your soles. As the monk prepared to answer, the Master gave a shout. He then examined yet another monk, saying, "The Hua Yue Mountains split open, their beauty reaching the heavens;
the Yellow River flows forth, its clarity to the very bottom. Setting that aside for a moment, speak on the ground of reality."
"Come with a single phrase. When the monk prepared to open his mouth, the Master struck him. The Master used scolding, rebuking, and harsh words as a most compassionate instruction for his disciples;
he acted in ways that did not conform to worldly sentiment to practice the Great Public Way. When guests and friends visited, he never discussed trivial matters of the world.
Setting aside the Great Dharma, he would not utter a single word. Thus, he possessed the essential style of a true patriarch.
This master’s pedagogical skill inherited the authentic transmission of Linji; he was the sole disciple of Zang-sou.
On the fourth day of the eighth month of the Xinsi year of the Zhizheng era, he passed away in his quarters. Five days prior, he manifested a slight illness.

Four days later, having bathed and changed his robes, he sat in the lotus posture and wrote this verse: "Fundamentally there is no birth or death, so how could there be going or coming? The ice-river... [emits light].

When the flowers of the *yàn tiě* (flame-iron) tree bloomed, he cast aside his writing brush, extended one leg, and passed away. His remains were kept in a shrine for seven days, his countenance appearing as if alive.

His entire body was enshrined in a stupa behind the temple named Jizhao (Tranquil Illumination). A portion of his fingernails and hair was divided and enshrined in a stupa at Huanyou-an (Monastery of Illusory Existence) in Facheng.
He was eighty-eight years old in secular age and seventy-six in monastic seniority.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Dongsou Ying of Jingci:
Chan Master Yishan Liaowan of Jiangxin, Wenzhou. His clan was the Jin of Linchuan. He was thin and physically frail in appearance.
At the age of fifteen, he gained renown for his proficiency in composing formal essays. However, his original aspiration was to leave the household life;

he went to Siren at Changle Monastery in Jinxī to receive the tonsure. Later, while traveling to pay his respects to various masters, he found that Yǎnxī, Jīngsǒu Jué, and Jiǎnwēng Jìng were all in accord with his views.
When Dōngsǒu led Nanpíng, Zhésī served as the *jìshī* (recorder). Once, while passing by a shrine to a deity, he saw paper ashes swirling with the wind.

Upon rising, he was suddenly liberated and forgot what he had realized. He immediately informed Dong-sou (Dongshou), who questioned him without any impediment. Later, while traveling to Tiantai, the assembly requested that he open the Dharma at Hanyan.
He subsequently moved to Zituo and Shushan in Xianju. Not long after, the General Superintendent of Jianghuai gathered the masters of various mountains at the Zhizhi Hall of Lingyin Monastery;
they deliberated and invited him to take up residence at Kaixian. He then ascended to the abbacy of Jiangxin. For a short time...

Feeling dissatisfied, he departed immediately. Although several hundred members of the monastic community earnestly entreated him to stay, he followed them as far as Fenggong Ling (Deer King Pass) before refusing to remain.
Layun Moon-River Ming invited him back to Dongxi. When Layun Ming passed away, the assembly at Kaixian again made their request, saying:

"We do not dare trouble you, Master, with the affairs of the temple; we only beg for your instruction of our disciples. He ascended the hall and said: "In stillness, there is emotion; in clamor, there is vastness. It is all..."
Without traversing the rungs of a ladder, one has already stepped onto the upward path. Ten thousand miles without a blade of grass; as soon as one leaves the gate, it is all grass.
Meeting the wood-seller is meeting the old man who plants pine trees. The moon is full in the crystal palace;
the sun shines brightly upon the coral branches. [Ascending the hall: "If you encounter Yao or Shun, present the 'Canons and Proclamations' to establish your livelihood; if you meet Jie or Zhou..."
The Way annihilates and sweeps away all worldly livelihoods. People like us are dry, parched, hard, bare, naked, and starkly clear.
When has there ever been so much ado? It is truly strange that when Chan Master Chen saw a monk enter the gate, he would immediately say, "This is a ready-made case;
I grant you thirty blows. Look closely at this, and it too is merely a desperate stratagem born of necessity. [He ascended the hall.]
Holding up his staff, he said: "This staff was wielded by the Seven Patriarchs of the Western Heaven and the Two or Three Patriarchs of this Eastern Land;
yet all the old masters of the world could not manage it. Today, it is in the hands of Kaixian—headless and tailless, capable of both releasing and gathering."
"Free from characteristics and free from names, neither giving nor taking. Although it is thus, this is only for those of middling and lower capacities.
When someone of the highest caliber suddenly arrives, what then? [He] drew a single line and said, "I let this one pass.
On the twenty-sixth day of the eleventh month in the first year of Huangqing, he fell ill. After seven days, he prepared his bath, changed his robes, and wrote his final instructions to the assembly.

He spoke thus and passed away while seated. Upon cremation, there were countless five-colored *śarīra* relics, each the size of a soybean. His two eyeballs, teeth, and cranial bone remained entirely unburnt.

At that time, the *ūṣṇīṣa-caitya* was rebuilt at Wuzha in Yuzhang. The Imperial Preceptor (Chengxiang) Gan’er of the Jiangxi Provincial Administration ordered that the relics of Śākyamuni preserved from the former site be enshrined within it.
He then dispatched an envoy to divide one of the mountain’s eyeball-relics [to be enshrined elsewhere].
[He] was interred in a silver casket as an accompaniment to his funeral.
*Fenghua Yuelin Yudang Yi Chan Master* was a native of Wenzhou.

He appeared in the world at Tianning in Wuyi, then moved to Jianfu, later presided over Taiping in Mingzhou, and ascended to Zhangsheng before reaching Yuelin. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "Luzu faced the wall."
Magu closed his door. Although these two great elders lived several hundred years apart from Tianning, today each is given twenty blows of the staff.
Why is this? It is like making a lamp or candle from oil and wax; without being lit by fire, it will never be bright.

Addressing the assembly: "Sons, you cannot guarantee that your exhalation will be followed by an inhalation. During the twelve periods of the day and night, do not at all employ your body and mind for miscellaneous purposes elsewhere.
Even if you were to swing your arms about, that would still be the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West;
even if your foot were pointed, it would kick out a venerable Buddha. It is better, however, to have nothing to do. Ascending the hall: An ancient said, "I have no dharma to give here..."
People merely settle cases based on the facts of the matter. Even the Sage had no dharma to give people, nor did he settle cases based on the facts.
He held up his staff and asked, "What is the Buddha? [He replied,] "Barefoot, treading upon lotus flowers.

"What is the matter beyond the Buddha? [He replied,] "Carved beams and painted rafters. He then threw down the staff and returned to the abbot's quarters. On the fifteenth day of the second month, [he spoke thus].

[He ascends] the hall. He strikes the whisk once and says: "Today, Zhangsheng will cause a single black bean to burst forth from the cold ashes of thirty years ago, replacing the eyes of the old barbarian. He lets out a shout and says:
"If there were a dharma that surpassed nirvana, this one shout of mine would not function as a mere shout. [He ascends] the hall. He cites the story of Huanglong’s Three Barriers.
The Master held up his whisk and said: "Old man Huanglong has a flat head; that is why he speaks the dialects of Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Fujian so authentically.
He can deceive everyone in the world, yet he cannot deceive the people of Zhangzhou, Quanzhou, and Fujian.

Entering the hall, he pointed to his left and said, "That is the incense burner," and pointed to his right and said, "That is the flower vase. One is able to take a single meaning and manifest it as immeasurable meanings; one is able to take immeasurable...
The meaning is a single meaning. Master Chen weaves straw sandals; Master Deng beats a clay drum. Entering the hall, he said:
"All things that exist in the world are none other than the wondrous, luminous, original mind of Bodhi. When *shípí* enters the water it becomes dry; when it emerges from the water it becomes wet.
*Dúhuó* does not move when there is wind, yet moves alone when there is no wind. Entering the hall, he said: "All you venerable elders, take your steps..."
"Taking steps is the place where you provide proof. You must personally accept it for yourself before you can return home and sit securely.

If it is not so, you will become a worm in a crab’s belly, or the eyes of a jellyfish. He ascended the hall and said, "The five thousand and forty-eight volumes of the scriptures can be spoken as a single phrase.
He then rose and said, "Stand here and wait for everyone to grasp it! He then descended from the seat. His final verse at the time of death:
It is said: "In the eighty-third year, what was its true nature? The cypress tree attained Buddhahood; empty space fell to the ground.
At his cremation, his teeth and rosary remained unharmed; the śarīra were brilliantly radiant."
○ Yunwu Zizhian Chan Master of Jinhua Zhizhe was of the Ye clan of Kuocang. His ninth-generation paternal uncle was the Venerable Xuetang Xing. Initially, [Xuetang] met Jing-sou at Lengquan;
subsequently, he met Dong-sou at Jingci, where he was appointed to serve as the *jishi* (record-keeper).

He composed the *Chengdao shu* (Discourse on Attaining the Way), which states: "He manifested his essential spirit in the middle of the night. Dong-sou changed the character "fa" (to manifest) to "yi" (to initiate).

"Min! At these words, the Master’s thighs involuntarily trembled and sweat poured from him as if a dam had been breached; he suddenly saw the old man’s place where he held out his hand through the dense thicket of ignorance.

From then on, he remained hidden within the Great Way, declining every successive invitation. Although both Sengcan of Shuanglin and Zhiyi of Zhizhe wielded the "iron axe," they were merely compelled by others to do so.
On the twenty-fifth day of the tenth month of the Renzi year of Huangqing, he conversed and laughed with his guests as usual.
Changshi (Changshui) instructed his attendant monk to fetch a brush. Having finished writing the verse, he passed away.
[End of section on] Chan Master Wufang An, successor to the Dharma of the Third Patriarch.
Chan Master Kumorong’s praise for the verse of the Third Patriarch says: "Wind-illness entangled his body and world; no one could cure it. His family was poor."
To encounter such robbery is even more pitiable; who would have known that when one seeks the culprit, there is nowhere to be found? This is precisely the moment the thief returns to the empty house.
The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Da-chuan Ji of Lingyin, Chan Master Lai of Shimen at Tiantong in Mingzhou, once composed a verse on scissors, which says: Forged from solid steel.
Cold light floats; two blades clash, refusing to cease. In directly confronting the situation to act for others, when has he ever moved so much as a single thread?
*The Chan Master Xuedou Yaoweng Bingtong of Siming was a native of Yuezhou. He saw off a monk departing for Huading.*
The monk Xixi composed a verse: Perched atop a high peak, towering amidst the clouds, This eighty-year-old river elder has eyes as empty as space.
When we meet, do not speak of traveling on pilgrimage; It would only burden his two ears and make them even more deaf.
The Dharma Heirs of Chan Master Wengxi of Mount Jing:
Chan Master Yunfeng Miaogao of Mount Jing, Hangzhou. He was a native of Changxi in Fuzhou. His family had been engaged in the study of Confucianism for generations.
His mother, Ruan, dreamed that she saw an infant sitting with palms joined upon the heart of a lotus flower on a pond; she reached out her hand and took him, and upon waking—

He was born in Shishi, and for this reason his pond was named Dream Pond. From childhood, his spiritual brilliance was outstanding; he was fond of books and applied himself diligently to study, with a particular devotion to the Buddhist scriptures.
Wishing to learn the supramundane Dharma, he relied upon Master Yunmeng Ze of Wuzhong and subsequently received full ordination.
The Master was keenly intent on the Way; he first consulted Chijue and later visited Wuzhun, who held him in especially high esteem. He then went to Yuyang to see Yancui.
He entered the room and took charge of the treasury keys. One day, Xuefeng said, "It is like a cow passing through a window lattice:

its head, horns, and four hooves have all passed through; why then can its tail not pass? The Master had a sudden realization and replied, "The whale swallows the ocean until it is empty, revealing the coral branches.
Xuefeng said, "You have only spoken half of it. Later, he emerged from seclusion to reside at Nan...

He established the Daliu Monastery, and subsequently moved to Jiangyin, Quanzhong, Zhechuan, Heshan, and Jingshan. When the seat at Jingshan was vacant, he accepted the imperial decree to reside there.

He remained for thirteen years, with his followers exceeding five thousand. In the first year of the Deyou era, when the Yuan army crossed the river, a soldier forced the Master to provide gold, threatening him with a blade.
The Master extended his neck and said, "If you wish to kill me, then kill me. As for me—"
The head was not your whetstone; his words and expression were entirely devoid of fear. The soldiers were moved and departed with their heads bowed.

When Minister Bayan saw the Master, he treated him with increased reverence, donating a hundred oxen and five hundred measures of grain for the monks' sustenance; the temple relied on this for its survival.
Later, when the Jingshan Temple suffered from a fire and was but one-tenth restored, the Master devoted himself wholeheartedly to its reconstruction, completing it all within less than ten years.
Returning to the original view, he addressed the assembly: "The preceding thought is ordinary; the succeeding thought is holy. Cut it in two with one stroke—do not hesitate even for a moment.
Therefore, at the assembly of Nirvana, the butcher Guang'e cast down his butcher’s blade and immediately declared, "I am counted among the thousand Buddhas.
Nevertheless, "Were it not for the strength to lift the cauldron and pull the mountain, the black steed of a thousand *li* would not be easy to ride. Thus he showed [the way].

The assembly: To discern the essential meaning before the words and to clarify the fundamental principle beneath the phrases—Mount Dongji blazes with the preaching of the Dharma, and the deep waters of the Zhu River are dedicated solely to its circulation.

If one attempts to grasp it here, one cannot avoid mutual stagnation. If there still remains the duality of observer and observed, one will be tossed about in a state of frantic agitation, like the crowing of the dawn cock and the tolling of the evening bell.
When ascending the hall, sound and form are the lethal poison of non-arising; sensation and perception are...
"The pitfall of the Perfect Man"—who does not know such talk? Yet coarse food satisfies easily, while chewing delicately makes one less hungry.
Entering the hall: Before the world had taken form, heaven and earth were in profound stillness; before Buddhas and sentient beings were manifested, the body was manifest as the absolute truth.

Without warning, the Great Being Jingrong leapt forth from his eagle’s nest and tore away his own mask; he had already been subjected to the brushstrokes of others’ depictions, yet that old bearded barbarian with missing teeth did not even act according to his own nature.
