[This is the record of] Chan Master Duansu Yuan of Mount Jing, a successor of the Dharma lineage.
Master Falin of Zhuanquan at Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou was styled Liaohan. His secular surname was Huang, and he was a native of Ninghai in Taizhou.
He left the household life under Chan Master Taiwu Tong of the same prefecture.
Upon contemplating the words of Muzhou, he attained realization and said to Taiwu, "From birth until death, it is simply this; it does not depend on anyone else. He then went to visit Yuan.
The Old Man was in Central India. He asked, "Where have you come from? The Master replied, "Tiantai. The Old Man said, "Have you ever seen Hanshan and Shide?

The Master joined his palms and stepped forward, saying, "Today I have personally seen the Venerable One. The Old Man said, "You are a man of empty talk and deception; go to the hall for the assembly.
He subsequently had him attend to the incense and later take charge of the storehouse keys. While he was reading the sutras, the Old Man said, "Reading sutras..."
The Master said, "Yes. The old man asked, "With what do you look? The Master replied, "I look with my eyes. The old man raised his fist and asked, "Why do you not say, 'I look with this'?
The Master said, "Put down your fist; with what will you look then? The old man smiled.

Dongyu invited him to Jingci Temple to share half his seat. At that time, Zhuyu was at Fushan and, having obtained the Master’s discourses on the teachings, praised them incessantly, subsequently honoring him with a verse that included the lines:
"Among a multitude of five hundred, he dwells as the leader; his wondrous understanding is fit to serve as a guide for devas and humans.
He resided in the Meng Hall of Jingci Temple and did not step outside his door for nine years. [The] Left Chancellor of the Provincial Administration...
Tuo Huan Gong invited him to preside over Wanshou Monastery in Zhejiang; he subsequently moved to Zhongtianzhu.

Later, in the fourth year of the Zhiyuan era, he was appointed to Lingyin Monastery, where his school of thought flourished greatly. Emperor Shundi bestowed upon him a golden-embroidered Dharma robe. At that time, Jizhao was at Mount Jing;
father and son were simultaneously proclaiming the Way, which the people of Wushan regarded as a great occasion. He ascended the hall and said: "The Dharma is the eternal Dharma; the Way is..."
The Constant Way presses against the gateway of the face; a single point and it is not reached.

Xuefeng, with his one thousand seven hundred enlightened disciples, spent morning and evening doing nothing but rolling three wooden balls. Zhaozhou, a veteran Chan practitioner of seven hundred years, would say to anyone he met, "Go and drink tea.
Zhongfeng Jujian, whenever he saw brothers visiting him, would do nothing but exchange pleasantries regarding their health and burn incense.
Xiang joined his palms. "If it were a golden-haired lion cub, he would surely have been at fault three thousand *li* away. He ascended the hall and raised the case:
A monk asked Zhaozhou, "When the myriad dharmas return to the One, where does the One return?
Zhaozhou said, "I made a cotton shirt in Qingzhou that weighs seven *jin*. The Master said, "Although Zhaozhou skillfully wielded the Great Sword to cut off this monk,"
[To say] "The tongue," is nothing less than exposing one's own family’s disgrace. At Lingyin, it is not so. Suppose a monk were to ask, "All phenomena return to One;
where does that One return? I would simply tell him: "Today is as hot as yesterday. On the occasion of the Lantern Festival, he ascended the hall and said:

"Today is the Yuanxiao Festival. After the snow has cleared, the spring sun appears. A thousand points of light in the Buddhist monastery; a single wheel of the moon in the vast sky. He struck the drum.

The bells clamor through the still night; songs and pipes disturb the neighbors. All this is the realm of universal penetration (*yuantong*); why need one seek another path? Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
"The entire Tripitaka consists of five thousand and forty-eight volumes—sudden and gradual, provisional and real, partial and complete.
Express it all in a single phrase, and the Buddhas of the three periods of time will be beneath your very feet. Ascending the hall, [the Master said]:
The famous mountain of Lingyin within the ancient Hangzhou jurisdiction was first established during the Xianhe era of the Eastern Jin dynasty. Dharma Master Huirui was its founding patriarch.
On this auspicious occasion of Shangyuan, lanterns are lit in various places; the administrative officers and the year-steward must each take care of the lamps and candles.
Having finished these instructions, he descends from his seat. The position at the Great Dragon Xiang Monastery is vacant; Grand Councilor Ji has sent gifts to invite [the Master] there.
The Master declined the invitation and did not go. The messenger went back and forth three times. The Master fled to Mount Kuaiji.

The Superintendent of the Monastery, realizing he could not compel him, prepared a formal petition requesting that the Master still take charge of Lingyin. He resided there for another three years before retiring to Liao-huan-an.

In the spring of the fifteenth year of the Zhizheng era, he was afflicted by a terminal illness. On the second day of the second month, he gathered his disciples and recounted the details of his life from beginning to end.
Furthermore, he admonished them, saying: "The decline of the Buddha-dharma has never been more severe than it is today. You should each exert yourselves. My worldly karmic conditions have ended here.
He took up his brush and wrote a verse: "Seventy-two years as a nail driven into empty space; the final phrase—unspeakable, unspeakable. Thereupon, he passed away suddenly.
His remains stayed in the shrine for ten days without change in color, and his entire body was enshrined in a tomb.
In front of the Western Pagoda at the Qiansongyuan Stūpa, an ancient cassia tree blossomed in spring, its fragrant scent filling the road. Those who saw it marveled at the marvel.
Because the Imperial Lecturer and Scholar Huang Gongjinjing witnessed this event with his own eyes, he recorded it himself within the preface to the stūpa inscription.
○ Chan Master Guding Zuming of Mount Jing in Hangzhou was surnamed Ying. His family had resided for generations in Fenghua, Siming.
He received full ordination under Master Xigong of Mount Heng at Jinye. Later, when Master Tanzhu of Tiantong invited him to serve as the Inner Record Keeper (Nairiki), he accepted the appointment.

Later, he traveled extensively to visit various venerable masters. When Yuansou was at Lingyin, the Master went there to follow him and inquire about the circumstances of Huanglong’s meeting with Ciming.

Yuansou questioned him, saying: "As for Zhaozhou’s statement, 'The old woman of Mount Tai has been exposed by me,' and Ciming’s laughter—tell me, do you say the application of these two elders was the same or different? The Master replied:
[The Master] held up a pair of iron hammers without holes. The Old Man said, "Even if one were to attain enlightenment directly beneath Huanglong, what then?

The Master said, "This too is like a person with diseased eyes seeing floating flowers. The Old Man said, "Not so, not so. As the Master was about to offer a word in response, the Old Man gave a shout.

The Master immediately attained a state of vast, open realization. He was then appointed to the position of Record Keeper (*jishi*). From that time on, his reputation spread rapidly, yet the Master maintained an ever-deepening sense of humility and self-restraint.
At the age of fifty-four, he first emerged from seclusion to preside over Longjiao Temple; subsequently, he moved to Baotuo, Zhongtianzhu, and finally Jingshan.

When the Imperial Preceptor heard of the flourishing of his Dharma assembly, he conferred upon him the title "Great Master Huixing Hongjue Pujie" (Wisdom-Nature, Vast Enlightenment, Universal Salvation). A monk asked:
"Is the meaning of the Patriarchs and the meaning of the Teachings the same or different? The Master said, "To break a bamboo basket and produce a broom.
The monk bowed and said, "Thank you for the instruction, Master. The Master said, "Last night at the third watch I lost my ox; when dawn broke and I arose, I had lost my fire as well."
A monk asked, "What is the Buddha? The Master said, "A weight dipped in vinegar. The monk asked, "What is the matter beyond the Buddha?
The Master said, "Looking up, one does not see the sky. The monk said, "I remember a monk asking Yunmen, 'What is the Buddha?
and Yunmen replied, 'A dried-up shit-stick. What about that? The Master said, "Yunmen was not being kind-hearted. The monk said, "A dried-up shit-stick."
"How far apart are the wooden stake and the scale-weight when they are dipped in vinegar? The Master said, "In the boiling cauldron, there is no place that is cold.
As the monk was about to offer a reply, the Master gave a shout. He entered the hall and said: "I will place the worlds of the ten directions upon the eyelashes of all of you;
not even a single hair’s breadth shall move. I will pour the waters of the four great oceans beneath the soles of your feet; not a single drop shall flow. Do you understand this medicine?"
"I have few ailments; knowing my lot, I do not grieve much. He ascended the hall and, citing Master Daguizhi, said to the assembly:
"Everyone gathers here to eat a spoonful of porridge. If you call it 'a spoonful of porridge,' you will enter hell as fast as a shooting arrow. The Master said:
The Master’s treatment of people was like that of a household infected by *gū* poison: he placed poison in their food and drink to give to them, never failing to desire to sever their life-roots.

Nevertheless, how many could there be who were his karmic adversaries? A single hair-tip might cause a disturbance, yet the Master governed the Miaoming Hermitage as he prepared for his final retirement.
On New Year’s Day, while offering prayers for blessings at the Provincial Government, three paths of white light appeared.
Prime Minister Keng-erh (Kangli) enshrined the image of Avalokiteśvara praised by the Master in the Ziwai Pavilion. That evening, auspicious light shone brilliantly.

When the Ge-lao tribesmen set fire to and plundered Mount Jing, the Prime Minister invited the Master to Yunju within the prefectural city. There, he frequently visited the Master to inquire about the profound principles of the Chan school.
One day, while they were reading the scriptures together, the Prime Minister asked, "Elder, why do you not read the scriptures? The Master replied, "I am following the lines."
"Are you counting the characters as you read the sutra? The Chancellor remained silent. The Master turned the sutra over and said, "The old monk is going to read the sutra.
The Chancellor covered the sutra with his hand and said, "Please explain it for me. The Master replied, "Who were Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou?
Zhong Tianzhu Yong Zhenliang remarked that the Master had previously propagated the Dharma at Mount [Isan] and invited him to return to Liao-huan-an.
Shortly thereafter, he manifested illness and sent a letter entrusting the Chancellor with his protection. He wrote a verse, saying: "Birth and death are pure and true;
the great void is perfectly full. At seventy-nine years, the cradle rope has snapped. Having cast down his brush, he passed away.
Chan Master Mengtang Tanne from Guoqing Temple in Taizhou styled himself You’an. He was the son of Wang of the Wuxing lineage in Cixi;
his mother was surnamed Zhou. His father passed away when he was six years old, and his mother sent him to study under a local schoolmaster.

Possessing a lofty and expansive spirit, he had the ambition to travel a thousand li in a single day. Upon reaching adulthood, he exhaustively studied the Confucian classics until he penetrated their essential marrow, and he devoted himself to the art of writing.

During his years of cultivation on the Path, Hu Xiansheng Changru eventually felt a profound sense of inspiration within his heart and said, "To study books and refine one's rhetoric is merely a worldly phenomenon.
Why not seek the Dharma that transcends the world? He then informed his mother, traveled to Guangfa Monastery in Fenghua, and took Master Liang as his teacher.
Seeking the Way throughout the regions of Wu and Chu, he crossed the Yangtze River and stayed at Zhenzhu’s Changlu Snow Court.
The Master of the Temple possessed discerning judgment; recognizing the master’s capacity and insight, he shaved his hair.

At that time, the master was already twenty-three years of age. He subsequently received full ordination. Regarding all Buddhist scriptures and the texts of the various schools, he studied them day and night, unaware of hunger, thirst, cold, or heat.
After a long time, he again sighed, saying: "The characteristics of the teachings are like the ocean; if one clings to them without turning back, this is merely seeking..."
One binds oneself with ropes; how can this compare to seeking the clarity of one’s original mind? Yuan-sou arrived at Lingyin from Central India;
his monastic style was lofty, and none but those of long-standing study dared to venture through his gate. The Master went directly to consult him, showing no fear or hesitation.

Their spiritual resonance was immediate, and he was appointed to oversee internal records. When Jingshan Xuguzhen selected a secretary, he chose the Master, bringing joy to both the clergy and the laity. Upon his arrival—
In the fifth year of the Yuan era, he went to serve as abbot at Xiansheng in Siming, and subsequently moved to Kaishou in Cixi. The Imperial Preceptor bestowed upon him the title "Buddha-Zhen Wen-yi.

In the seventeenth year of the Zhizhi era, the Xuanzheng Yuan appointed him to Qingliang Temple and Ruilong Temple, changing their status from hereditary lineages (jia-yi) to the ten-directional system (shifang).
The Master served as the founding abbot of these monasteries, through which they gained renewed prestige. Ascending the hall, he held up his whisk and said: "Just this—"
In the Linji school, there is the great capacity and great function; rolling up and unfolding, seizing and releasing, killing and giving life are all exercised with freedom.
In the Yunmen school, there is solitary peril and towering loftiness; holding fast beyond the norm, one settles the matter before a word is spoken.

In the Caodong school, the family style is subtle and meticulous; golden needles and jade thread meet clearly and are cast in secret. In the Guiyang school, there is paternal kindness and filial piety; they employ the edge of the sword.
The act of giving is a trap for tigers; in the Eye of the Dharma, arrow-points meet. When the mind is empty, phenomena are exhausted, emotions are spent, and views are eliminated.
The proclamations of the Five Houses—like the ringing of metal and jade—surpass the ancients and transcend the present; these are all merely expedient arrangements of the school’s gate.
Yet, as for that direct single phrase, it has never been spoken. What is this direct single phrase? [He] cried out in a stern voice: "Look!"
[The Master] stepped down from his seat and ascended the hall. "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven; seven, six, five, four, three, two, one.
The Yellow River winds nine times as it emerges from Kunlun. Mahāprajñāpāramitā. The Master frequently admonished his disciples, saying: "I and you all must investigate and clarify this Way.
You should cast aside concern for your physical bodies and focus your will upon sleep and food to eliminate the habitual tendencies accumulated over kalpas. However—"
Thereafter, his mind-ground was luminous. From then on, he took only one meal a day and sat in meditation throughout the entire night until dawn.

In the third year of the Hongwu era of our dynasty’s founding, an imperial edict summoned eminent monks from Jiangnan, and the Master was ranked foremost among them. He was lodged at Tianjie Monastery;
after his audience with the Emperor, the Sovereign took pity on the Master’s advanced age and granted him permission to return to the mountains. In his later years, by means of the Liang...
The *Biographies of Eminent Monks of the Tang and Song Dynasties* was further revised and edited; woodblocks were carved to disseminate it.

On the day of Jiashen in the second month of the sixth year, he suddenly requested a bath and changed his robes without illness. He brought forth various articles as a legacy for his great friends and assembled the community, saying:
"The three realms are like empty flowers, swept away by the wind; the delusive shadows of the six sense objects are like ice being melted by boiling water. My illusory body now..."
"Upon my passing into extinction, after my cremation, let my bones be reduced to dust. Do not erect a stupa to burden future generations.
Having spoken these words, he closed his eyes and sat upright until he passed away. He was eighty-nine years of age.
Master Chan Shi Banchi of Tianning Monastery in Jiaxing was a native of Xiangshan in Siming. His secular surname was Zhu, and his mother’s surname was Zhang.
While the Master was still in his swaddling clothes, a monk came to see him and said to his father, "This child is the Sun of the Buddha."
He will surely shake the Buddha-dharma and illuminate this turbid age. Because of this, his fellow villagers came to call him Tanyao.

He followed his paternal great-uncle, Master Jinweng Xun, who was preaching at Chong'en Temple on Lake Hu; the Master went there to follow him. When Duke Zhao Wei saw him, he regarded him with exceptional esteem and provided the funds for him to purchase the ordination certificate to become a monk.
Subsequently, he received full ordination (*upasampadā*). When Master Jinweng moved to another site of practice, the Master served as his attendant once again.

While serving as the librarian, he read through the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* until he reached the passage: "Conditioned by seeing, with light as the cause, darkness becomes non-seeing. At this, he had a sudden realization.

From then on, his reading of both Buddhist and secular classics was as if it were the result of lifelong habit. Yet, he still experienced moments of mental obstruction. When Yuanzou, the abbot of Mount Jing, visited him, he immediately asked:
"What is that which issues speech yet is not sound, and stands before forms yet is not an object? Yuanzou replied instantly: [He said: "... (The text here implies the master's response).
When the Master spoke, his voice was not sound and his form was no longer an object before him. "Quick, speak! Quick, speak! the old man roared a single shout as he prepared to answer;

the Master was struck with consternation and withdrew. Later, when Emperor Yingzong issued an edict to transcribe the Great Canon in gold letters, the authorities selected the Master for his skill in calligraphy and sent him up to the capital.
One night, hearing the drums of a festive tower strike, he attained sudden and great enlightenment. Striking the table, he laughed and said: "The direct path..."
I have already discerned the point where Mount [Shan] failed. Thus, he composed a verse: Outside the Chongtian Gate, the drums roll on;
Suddenly, the void collapses upon the earth. Shide gathers a single spark of snow from the red furnace; It is but the ice of the Yellow River in the sixth month. He then flew eastward to Shuangjing.
As he arrived, the Elder welcomed him with a smile and said, "I am glad that you have already realized the secret meaning of the West."

He attained this realization and was immediately appointed to the second seat. He first resided at Fuzhen in Haiyan, then ascended to Yongzuo, and subsequently moved to Baoguo in Hangzhou, Benjue in Jiaxing, and Tianning.
A monk asked him: "One need not worry that thoughts arise; one only fears that awakening is slow."
"What is awakening? The Master said, "The horns of an ox; the horns of a horse. The monk asked, "What is mindfulness?
The Master said, "He does not even know that four times five is twenty. The monk bowed. A monk asked, "The entire Great Canon of Teachings is a 'cutting foot' (a radical or suffix).
I wonder what character it cuts? The Master said, "It cuts the character 'not' (bù). The monk asked, "As for the character 'not,' what then does it cut?"
"What [is it]? The Master said, "Do not mistakenly present this to others. The monk said, "Thank you for the instruction.
The Master said, "Look toward the east at the head of the stone ram. A monk asked, "All Buddhas and the *anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi* dharma of all Buddhas emerge from this sutra.
What is this sutra? The Master said, "Do you need a commentary on that as well?"

Ascending the hall, he said: "Maitreya is truly Maitreya; he manifests a thousand, ten thousand, even a hundred million bodies. From time to time he reveals himself to those of this age, yet the people of this age do not recognize him.
He took up his staff and said: "It pierces through the azure void where pines reach a thousand feet; it cuts off the red dust of the world as a single stream of water flows through a ravine."
Ascending the hall: "In rice there are worms; in wheat there is flour.

The kitchen, the storehouse, the monks' hall, the mountain gate, and the Buddha hall—when the tea bowl falls to the ground, the saucer breaks into seven pieces. Ascending the hall: "The forge is filled with dull iron;
the physician’s door is crowded with the sick. Were it not for Liu Yi transmitting the letter, how could one have reached Lake Dongting? Ascending the hall.
"Hearing sound to realize the Way blocks your ears; seeing form to clarify the mind replaces your eyes.
Seated upright upon his meditation cushion, threading a needle through its eye—when a gust of western wind arrives, two or three leaves fall.
In his later years, he built the Xizhai (West Chamber) at Yongzuo and spent the remainder of his life there, hence styling himself the "Elder of the West Chamber. The first year of the Hongwu era...
In the ninth month of that year, the Sovereign reflected that his generals and ministers might perish on the battlefield, and his subjects might die by the sword;

he deemed it appropriate to employ the teachings of the Śākya school to perform rites for the deceased in order to deliver them. He established a Great Dharma Assembly at Mount Zhongshan and summoned masters to preach the Dharma.

The court officials presented this account to the Emperor, who was greatly pleased. In the third month of the following year, he again summoned the Master to preach the Dharma, following the precedent of the first year.
In the autumn of the year after that, the Emperor once more summoned the Master to inquire about ghosts and spirits.

The Master, together with the other masters who had been summoned, cited the sūtras and śāstras to investigate and verify the principles of the matter. Having completed the work, they were about to enter the palace to present it for imperial deliberation when the Master—
Suddenly manifesting a slight illness, he requested a bath and changed his robes. Taking up a brush, he wrote a verse: "The true nature is perfectly luminous;
fundamentally there is no arising or ceasing. A wooden horse neighs at night; the sun rises in the west. Setting down the brush, he said to Mengtang, "Elder brother, I am going."
Daitō asked, "Where are you going? The Master replied, "I am going to the West. Daitō asked, "Is there a Buddha in the West, but none in the East?
The Master then let out a thunderous roar and passed away. This was indeed on the twenty-sixth day of the seventh month.

When the Ministry of Rites reported his final verse to the Emperor, His Majesty expressed deep lamentation. Monastics and laypeople alike came to pay their respects as if attending the *parinirvāṇa* of a Buddha at Tien-chieh Monastery.
The Abbot Baian was the Dharma-son of [the Master]. To manage his final affairs, he established the practice of cremation at that time.
For the sake of his teacher, the Emperor specifically granted the precedent for cremation within the monastic community.

After the cremation, the teeth and the prayer beads remained undamaged, and *śarīra* relics were scattered throughout the remains. The disciples took the remains back to the West Chamber to bury them and erect a stupa. His age was seventy.
15. [Record] 63. ○ Chan Master Yuguan Zhiyi of Mount Jing in Hangzhou, whose courtesy name was Yizhong and alternative style was Xilu. He was of the Gu clan of Wuxian County, Suzhou;
his father was Maoqing and his mother was Zhou. He entered Haiyun Monastery as a novice, where he studied Buddhist and Confucian texts.
The two texts were presented together. When Duke Qingxian of Min, Du Zhong, saw them, he specifically praised them as extraordinary.

He invited Master Xian to lecture on the *Fajie guan* (Contemplation of the Dharma Realm) at his residence; before the chapter was finished, the Duke smiled broadly and said, "The single true Dharma realm is the perfect penetration of the great void.
As soon as it involves words and phrases, it becomes a superfluous teaching. Thereupon, he departed and went to visit Guangzhi at Longxiang Temple, where he briefly revealed his literary talent.
Cai Guangzhi was greatly astonished. A man from an island nearby rebuked him, saying, "With such brilliant talent as yours, do you not consider the burden of the Great Dharma?
Are you content to be a mere servant of poetry and prose? He asked, "What is meant by the 'fluttering yellow leaves' in the verse of the Lamp of Endlessness?
Master [Cai] was silenced and unable to answer. He immediately returned to Haiyun, his chest feeling as if obstructed by a great weight.
Shi. After more than a month, he suddenly saw autumn leaves blowing down into the courtyard. He experienced a sudden, expansive realization (*satori*).

Though his joy was beyond measure, fearing that he might fall into partiality or dogmatic attachment if he did not seek verification from those with "clear eyes" (*myōgen*), he went to see Jingshan. Jingshan examined and interrogated him; the Master’s responses were unhindered.

Jingshan subsequently appointed him as an attendant. After a long time, he was promoted to head the Library (Zangshi). In the *Renwu* year of the *Zhengding* era, the Provincial Military Commission...
The Master was invited to appear in the world at Changguo Longjiao Temple and later transferred to Puci Temple.

Not long after, the Left Chancellor of the Provincial Administration, Lord Dashih, invited him to preside over Jingci Temple, and subsequently requested that he ascend to Mount Jingshan. A monk asked, "Speech is slander; silence is deception.
Beyond speech and silence, there is something further. What is this thing beyond? The Master said, "A monkey climbing a tree, its tail trailing over its head."
A monk asked, "What is the guest within the guest? The Master said, "You head toward Xiangxiang; I head toward Qin.
The monk asked, "What is the host within the guest? The Master said, "Always on the road, yet never leaving home. The monk asked, "What is the guest within the host?
The Master said, "Always at home, yet never leaving the road. The monk asked, "What is the host within the host? The Master said:
Holding the Mo-ye sword crosswise, he maintains the perfect and upright command; throughout the realm of Great Peace, he slays the dull and obstinate.
One day, Chancellor Da-shi-tie-mu-er arrived at the abbot’s quarters and asked, "The chamber of Vimalakīrti accommodated thirty-two thousand lion thrones;
how many can this chamber of Jingci accommodate? The Master replied, "Not a single speck of dust is established. The Chancellor said, "You have attained such a state of direct manifestation."

[The Master] went against [the expectation]. The Master lifted the curtain and said, "I request the Prime Minister to observe. The Prime Minister laughed heartily and said, "A master of the ancestral school;
no need for further examination. The Master then served tea. He ascended the hall and, citing Dongshan Yanzu’s address to the assembly, said:
"The Patriarchs could not describe it; the Buddhas cannot see it. With a grandmotherly heart on all four sides, I shall open a single thread for you. The Master said:
"If one were to shed tears incessantly as instructed, even the vast blue sea would surely dry up. [He] ascended the hall and said: "Today, in all quarters, the hearth is opened.
We cannot help but speak some words concerning the head of the brazier to you all. He then made the gesture of blowing on a fire with his whisk and said:
"If you call it 'fire,' it will burn you to death; if you do not call it 'fire,' it will freeze you to death. [He] ascended the hall and said: "One, two, three, four, five, six, seven."
Earth, water, fire, wind, space, awakening, and consciousness—when brought forth, they are very clear for several days. Yet even a monk with clear eyes cannot count them;
how truly marvelous! A black dragon drills through a ruined wall; a rooster crows at the fifth watch.

In the *Guichou* year of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict summoned more than ten eminent masters of the Way to assemble at Tianjie Monastery. The Master was at their head, but due to illness, he did not attend the summons.
It was so. He returned to Qionglong Mountain, which is Haoyun. On the eighth month of the Wu-wu year, he suddenly manifested illness.
On the fourth day of the ninth month, he requested a brush and wrote a verse, after which he passed away. His disciples enshrined his remains at the foot of Mount Haoyun;
they also divided his nails and hair to return to Jing Mountain, where they were interred to the left of the stupa of Chan Master Wu dengcai. He was sixty-eight years of age.
51. Chan Master Xingzhong Zhiren of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou styled himself Danguzi (The Recluse of Simplicity) and was also called Xiyesi (The Elder of Joyful Serenity).
He was of the Wu clan of Fanyang; his father, Zhonghua, served as a Professor of Confucian Studies at Jiangzhou. When the Master was five years old, his...
His father sent him to follow Master Chun of Baeon Temple in the state. At the age of seven, he received full ordination.

From childhood, his insight was exceptionally sharp and far surpassed that of ordinary children. When the Indian master Jigong (Zhiyuan) traveled to the capital at the invitation of Emperor Yingzong, he stayed at Baeon Temple on his way.
Seeing the Master, he marveled at him, saying, "You are a teacher of gods and men for two lifetimes. He consequently conferred the precepts upon him.

When the Dharma Master received the *Mārīcī* mantra, the Abbot bestowed upon him the title of "True Herdsman" and instructed him to go to Jingshan to attend on Yuanzou. Upon seeing the Master, Yuanzou laughed heartily;

the Master, not knowing why, broke into a cold sweat that soaked his back and forgot to spread out his sitting mat (*niṣīdana*). Yuanzou rebuked him, saying, "Enter the hall! (i.e., attend the assembly).
He departed. On the following day, he saw him again. The old man asked, "Where are you from? The Master replied, "From Fanyang.

The old man asked, "How deep is Lake Fanyang? How wide is it? The Master extended his hands, making a gesture as if measuring it. The old man said, "Not so, not so. The Master said, "Shut that stinking mouth!
Thereupon, the old man retained him to serve the incense and subsequently entrusted him with the position of Chief Recorder (Waiji). Delighted to have found such a master, he spoke to his disciples.

It is said: Master Ren was one who possessed the body of a tiger and the wings of a bird. He emerged from the world to manifest his virtuous brilliance, successively residing at Yiqi in Qi, Yunding in Yue, Chongbao in Su, and Huqiu Wanshou.
During a time when the Dharma-way had declined and positions were sought through worldly gain, the Master alone devoted himself to remaining hidden and obscure.
Yet he visited all five famous monasteries only because high-ranking officials earnestly urged him to do so. Thus, whenever he appeared, everyone held him in the highest esteem. The Master—
In his room, he picked up a wooden pillow and asked a monk, "What is this? The monk said, "I know the Master’s compassionate heart is most earnest.
The Master threw the pillow to the ground; as the monk hesitated, the Master shouted and sent him out.
One day he said, "The nature of all sentient beings is pure and clear; why do they transmigrate through the six realms? At that time, a monk said, "I pray that the Master..."
The Compassionate One gave this instruction: The Master said, "The mouth of the alms bowl points toward heaven. Entering the hall, he held up his whisk and said, "This is the家风 (house style) of Mazu.
He let out a shout and said, "This is the house style of Linji. With the whisk, he drew a line and said:

"What kind of tradition is this? If you go to other places, do not misrepresent it. He ascended the hall and said: "Layer upon layer, the distant mountains are green; far-reaching, the river waters are verdant.
All day long at the Xiao-wu Pavilion, leaning on the railing, one can never look enough. Suddenly he called to his attendant, "Take up the whisk," and then descended from the seat.
He ascended the hall again and said: "The nature of Chan is non-arising; leave behind thoughts of Chan that involve arising. Chan...
The nature has no abiding; it is detached from dwelling in meditative stillness. On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a "dog-urine sky.

At the top of the *khaṭvāṅga* banner, a *zhuanzi* is being fried; three monkeys toss coins at night. The Master was conversant with non-Buddhist classics and was particularly profound in the *I Ching*.
His writings were intended solely to rectify his school, and he did not take pride in them himself, much like Yu Wen.
Wang Jinggong’s collection [of writings] was praised by Huang Wenxian Gong Qin, Zhang Lugu Gong Zhu, Song Shijiang Lan, and others.
When Wenjing saw Master [Fengxiu’s] "Record of the Hall of Su Wenzhong Gong at Sixian Temple in Huangzhou," he remarked:

"His prose is concise and profound, possessing the style of the Western Han. Lugu once sent him a poem, which included the lines: "In this age, the venerable elder of Nengren spreads his lofty reputation..."

Regarding the verse on the "Seashore": At the beginning of the Hongwu era of our present dynasty, His Majesty summoned the elders of the Śākya school to inquire about the principles of ghosts and spirits.
The Master and those summoned with him said, "The discourse on ghosts and spirits should be answered by taking the Buddha’s intent as the foundation.
When they presented their written response, the Emperor was greatly pleased. In his later years, the Master lived in leisure at a hermitage (aranya) amidst pine forests.
His reputation for the Way grew increasingly venerable; no one dared to address him by name, and all referred to him as "Master Songlin.

In the third month of the fifteenth year, he suddenly manifested illness. On the nineteenth day, his fellow practitioner Ruyi Zhong came to inquire after him, saying, "Elder brother, the time has arrived.
With your disciples standing by your side, would you not deign to grant us a word as your final instruction? The Master—
He said, "The Bhagavāns of the ten directions share one path to the gate of Nirvāṇa. He continued, "I have been close friends with you for fifty years;
let us part now so that we may meet again only in the Pure Land. The Master replied in a stern voice, "The entire great trichiliocosm is a single Pure Land;
where would we not meet? After a long silence, he asked for paper and, having written a verse, passed away peacefully at the age of seventy.
14. [Record No. 670. Chan Master Fu Yuanfubao of Jing Mountain, Hangzhou.
A native of Ninghai, Tai prefecture. His secular surname was Fang, and his mother was surnamed Zhang.
At the command of his parents, he went to Chongfu Temple at Liangzhu in Hangzhou to enter the monastic life. At that time, there was the Venerable Mei of Shihu.

The master [Deshan] was at Jingci. The teacher went there to visit him; Lake (Huhai) took a liking to him and shaved his head for him. The lineage of Yuansou of Mount Jingshan was rigorous and austere.
Because the teacher had not yet clarified his own matter, he went there to seek resolution. Yuansou asked, "Where have you recently departed from? The teacher replied, "Jingci."
The old man asked, "What have you come for? The Master said, "I have long admired the Venerable’s Way, so I have come specifically to pay my respects.
The old man asked, "When Zhaozhou met Nanquan, what did he do? The Master said, "He stood with his head touching the heavens and his feet treading the earth.
The old man asked, "And after that meeting, what was it like? The Master said, "When hungry, I eat; when tired, I sleep. The old man asked, "Where did you learn this pretense?"
"Come," the Master said. "Today I have personally seen the Venerable. The Old Man nodded his head. The following day, he was appointed to the office of Attendant.
The next year, he was promoted to oversee the library of the teachings. After a long time, he entered the world at Lushan in Cixi, and subsequently moved to Dongshan and Mingmen in Zhenjiang.
At the beginning of the Hongwu era of the Imperial Dynasty, śramaṇas of eminent conduct were summoned by imperial decree; the Master and Yizhong of Mount Jing were among them.
Shangzhu Rizhang went to Tianjie Temple in the capital. He entered the inner court several times, responding to the Emperor’s inquiries to his satisfaction.

After staying for three years, he was granted leave to return to Zhimen, where he built a hermitage to the east of the temple and named it Haiyin (Ocean Seal), intending to spend the remainder of his life there.

When the seat at Jingshan became vacant, the Emperor summoned the Master to fill the position. Upon ascending the hall, he gave this discourse: "If you raise one, you cannot grasp two; if you raise two, you let go of one."
To fall into the second [alternative]—when the ancients spoke thus, they were truly like those who embrace their own stolen goods while crying out for innocence.
Dongshan was not so: he would not allow both to be raised, but would let one pass. To fall into the first [alternative] is to fall into the seventh.
At this point, you must know that there is a path leading upward; only then will it suffice. "What is the path leading upward? After a long silence, he said: "Do not remain."

Green grass grows strangely upon the cold crags; sitting amidst white clouds, the essence of the school is not subtle. Entering the hall, he said: "When a single leaf falls, autumn comes to all under heaven.
When a single speck of dust rises, the great earth is gathered up. Who says that Northern Uttarakuru is not Southern Jambudvīpa? One has already mounted the ox, yet seeks the ox further.
Entering the hall, he said: "Speech is slander; silence is deception. Is there anyone who does not involve themselves in either?"

“Ma! [The Master] struck the meditation seat and said, “I almost let the prisoner remain in custody too long. Ascending the hall, he said: “One silence, one word, one action, one cessation—how is this different from mercury falling to the ground?
A monk asked Zhaozhou, “I beg the Master for instruction.

Zhaozhou said, “Have you finished eating your gruel yet? The monk said, “I have finished eating my gruel. Zhaozhou said, “Go wash your bowl. Ascending the hall, he said: “All day long, one puts on clothes.”
Never has a single thread been attached; all day long he eats his meals, yet never chews a single grain of rice.
Like the earth supporting a mountain without knowing its towering loftiness, or like a stone containing jade without knowing the jade’s flawlessness:
he does not seek the Buddha, he does not seek the Dharma, he does not seek the Sangha. He raises his staff; sometimes, riding upon the bright moon, he acts with deliberate spontaneity.
He passed through Cangzhou. Previously, while at Mount Xiangyuan, he had begun the construction of the Buddha Hall but died before its completion;
the Master completed it by his own effort. The expenses were provided by Ge Derun of Gusu. Having resided at Jingshan for barely eight years, one day he suddenly fell gravely ill.
When his attendant requested a verse, the Master rebuked him, saying, "I still have three more years of worldly life. Shortly thereafter—

Indeed, at the time of his passing, he was eighty-four years old and had spent sixty-four summer retreats. His disciples enshrined his whole body and interred it on a ridge to the right of Jizhao Pagoda.
○ Master Xingyuan Huiming of Lingyin Monastery in Hangzhou, whose alternative name was Hanyi, was a native of Huang [County] in Taizhou.
Yan Xiang’s mother was Chen. Having grown up, he was dissatisfied with living an ordinary life and went to rely upon Master Dongshan Lugu at Baoguan Monastery in Wenzhou to leave the household life.
He visited Master Zhuyuan Dao at Zituo Mountain in Xianju to inquire about the essentials of the mind, yet he did not achieve significant realization.
He then went to study under Master Yuansou of Mount Jing, who asked him, "Do you come from the eastern ridge or the western ridge? The Master pointed to the ground beneath his feet.
The straw sandals said, "These were bought for three copper coins. The old man said, "That is not it; speak further.
The Master said, "I am only like this; I do not know how you, the Master, would act. The old man said, "Out of consideration for your long journey, I shall let you off with thirty blows.
After a long time, he served as the incense attendant. Morning and evening he investigated the Way until one day he attained silent resonance. Xuechuang of Yuyang then invited the Master.
Zhang Cangjiao. Before long, he went forth to reside at Wufeng in Yinzhou and later moved to Jine.

In the spring of the fifth year of the Hongwu era, an imperial edict was issued for eminent monks throughout the realm to establish a great vegetarian assembly on Mount Zhongshan; the Master and Jitan of Mount Jing were both selected for this duty.
Once the ceremony was concluded, Jitan received the Imperial decree to reside at Tianjie Monastery and invited the Master to occupy the position of First Seat (*dizhuozuo*). He [the Master] then...

When the main ropes are raised, the essentials are secured, and one serves as a model for the monastic community. The following year, the Master was invited to occupy the seat at Jìnshān on Zhènjiāng.
In the eleventh year, he ascended to the position at Línghyìn. Disciples gathered like clouds, and his patriarchal style flourished greatly.

Entering the hall, he said: "Today is the first day of the intercalary fifth month; the sun rises from the eastern side as it has always done. Every patch-robed monk understands this; let us sing a short verse in response."
His long songs all accord with the musical laws. The plum rain has cleared; beneath the dense shade of the trees, one strolls at leisure.
What is there to gain or lose? The "True Person of No Rank" is but a lump of flesh. At ease, he topples over Vimalakīrti. When the Buddha ascended the hall for the discourse on Nirvāṇa, he said:
"Nirvāṇa and birth-and-death are equally empty flowers; 'Buddha' and 'sentient beings' are both superfluous words. When you people reach this point, what do you do?

At the Assembly for the Birth [of the Buddha], after a long silence, he struck the meditation seat and said: "One merely sees falling flowers carried away by the water; one does not know that they flow forth as the spring within the cave.
On the occasion of the Bathing of the Buddha, he ascended the hall and cited Master Xiangyan, who said: "Last year’s poverty was not yet true poverty; this year’s poverty is indeed true poverty.
Last year’s poverty still left room enough to plant a single awl; this year’s poverty, there is not even an awl. The assembly—
Suddenly, a man came forward and asked, "Venerable sir, you have made a mistake. Today is the eighth day of the fourth month, the Buddha’s birthday. How can you cite this public case?
The mountain monk replied simply, "The duties of the abbot are burdensome," and then descended from his seat.
When the Master first arrived, he planned the construction of the Great Hero Treasure Hall; in barely one year it was completed, standing majestically like a mountain. This was the Master's quarters.
Zhongchui said, "The Lotus Peak has been eaten away by ants on one side; why do you not know this?

He further said, "Setting aside for a moment the question of Cold Spring Pavilion swallowing Ravine Thunder Pavilion, when South Peak and North Peak compete for their foreheads, what stage of the spiritual mechanism is that?
Few have attained realization of it. He passed away in the sixth month of the nineteenth year of the Hongwu era.
The twenty-third day. Age sixty-nine; fifty summers.
○ Master Wufa Benwu of Shang Tianzhu, Hangzhou, was a native of Huangyan.

He received the tonsure at Fangshan in Jingci Monastery and relied upon Jizhao at Zhong Tianzhu, where he served as the administrator (*gangwei*). His maternal uncle, a venerable elder of the Confucian school, entreated him...

He changed his primary allegiance. Thereupon, he visited Zhantang at Yanfu Temple to study the profound sections of the doctrinal teachings. Jizhao lamented his departure and sent him a verse, saying:
"Entering Chan from the Teachings has occurred in both ancient and modern times; entering the Teachings from Chan has never existed since antiquity.
Though the gates of the One Mind and Three Contemplations differ, the moon remains solitary as it fills the thousand rivers. Later, when he appeared in the world, he served as Zhantang’s successor.
[The disciple] succeeded him. He continued to burn incense as an offering, for Jizhao did not allow his mind to be divided by differences in outward form.
When Jizhao passed away, the Master was residing at Yanqing in Siming. In a letter he sent, he urged him to diligently propagate the essential tenets of the Great Su [Linji] school;

there were no other words. At the memorial service, the Master held up the incense and said: "The fifth transmission of Miaoxi is the most brilliant flame; Jizhao’s single generation was sweet [and pure]."
The Gate of Manifestation: If you touch it casually, your liver and brain will shatter; Frost and ice suddenly turn into the warmth of spring.
I think back to the day my nostrils were struck away— What kind of breath remains to this day? The celestial wind blows from the north as the year draws to a close;
A flash of lightning seeks what trace could there be in the void? At the end of my life in this hut, I sat and shed my shell without illness.
Master Chanzhi Shanyu of Kaishan, Suzhou, a native of Wujiang, ascended the hall and said:
"The Buddha-body fills the Dharma-realm, universally manifesting before all sentient beings.

Why was it that when the residents of Hudu, followers of Huang-Lao, welcomed him, a tempestuous wind and waves surged up and the image immediately sank? [He asked] regarding Zhu Yingdong of Wu County and the nun Dongling Bo.
Upon a single invocation, the numinous forms appeared majestically and suddenly floated forth as a pair. When one attempted to lift and support them, they became, in an instant, a victorious vessel.
These are the stone images of Vimalakīrti and Kāśyapa currently enshrined within the mountain.

Is this not the manifestation of responding to conditions and fulfilling requests without exception, while eternally remaining upon this Bodhi seat? O Great Assembly, if you understand it in such a way, it is like a tiger looking at water.
"Polish it. Do not understand it in such a way. From Zhenzhou to Changlu, "suchness and non-suchness are both cast aside"—then what?
"In a world of peace and clarity, there is no need for deceptive speech. The Master’s movements were calm and deliberate; he did not utter words frivolously.

There were times when he was requested for verses; he would write them down as they came to him, each imbued with a spirit of admonition. For instance, he wrote to a monk at a thatched hut by the Changmen Gate:
"The National Teacher is a source of wisdom for ten thousand generations; the thatched hut on Mount Yandang is renowned throughout the world.

Those who are able to dwell within it should conceive the thought that such an encounter is difficult to find, and thus repay his profound kindness. Your ordination certificate has descended directly from the heavens; having obtained it," [he continues].
"Even if one were to offer ten thousand pieces of gold, if one does not cultivate the monastic practice during one's time, one will have betrayed the sincere heart of the Emperor and the King.
In his later years, the Master, following the Dharma-door, resided at Wanshou Temple with his disciples Huán and Yíngzhōng;

he cleared out a room to welcome them and support him in his old age. When Xiāng Běnkōng succeeded him on the seat, he treated him with even greater devotion. Thus, the Master was able to live in leisure and delight in the Way. Once...
He resided at Zhizhi An (Direct Pointing Hermitage) in Fengmen; people consequently called him Master Zhizhi.
As he approached his end, he summoned his disciples Benkong, Songlin, Zhen, Songshi, and others to bid them farewell, and then passed away in profound stillness.
Chan Master Tianjing Yuanjing of Lingyin Temple in Hangzhou was born into the Ni clan of Kuaiji.

In his youth, he followed Master Xueting Li at Zhide Temple to receive the tonsure. Upon receiving full ordination, he went to Jiqing Temple in Hangzhou to study *śamatha-vipaśyanā* under Master Tian'an Ji.
One day, the Master said to himself: "Many of the venerable elders of the past entered Chan through the teachings; I, too, shall investigate them."
This is the purport of the *Biézhuan* (Separate Transmission). He ascended Mount Huading to visit Wujiandu; furthermore, he visited Shi-shi Ying at Yujia.
When Ying spoke with him, he marveled greatly, saying, "My Dharma-uncle, the Venerable Yuansou of Jingshan, possesses the great eye of insight;
he is the Miaoxi of this age. If you wish to resolve the matter of your own person, go to see him and do not delay. Thereupon, the Master went to visit Yuansou.

At Budong Xuan (The Immovable Pavilion), as he entered the gate, an elder let out a thunderous shout. The Master was so startled that sweat poured down his back; he immediately performed three prostrations.
Subsequently, the elder appointed him to the office of attendant and later entrusted him with the duties of secretary. He then traveled to Jinling (Nanjing) to visit Xiaoyin at Longxiang Temple.

Proceeding up the Jiangxi region, he paid respects at the stupas and images of various patriarchs. Passing through Linchuan, he visited Lord Yu Wenjing, with whom he engaged in conversation and reached a profound spiritual accord.
He invited the Master to spend the summer retreat, for whom he composed the "Epitaph for the Duanjiang Pagoda" and the "Inscription for the Puyin Studio.

In the *bingshen* year of the Zhizheng era, he succeeded to the abbacy at Changqing in his native district and later moved to Tianyi. In the fifth year of the Hongwu era of the Sacred Dynasty, a Great Memorial Dharma Assembly was established at Mount Zhongshan;
an imperial decree summoned renowned venerable elders from throughout the realm to take turns occupying the seat to preach the Dharma, and the Master was among them. In the winter of the ninth year—

The various monasteries of Hangzhou invited him to reside at Lingyin. He declined four times, but everyone said, "Your grandfather Fozhao Miaofeng, your father Jizhao, and your elder brother Liaohan all preached the Dharma at Lingyin.
Now that you are reviving their fallen legacy and upholding the great principles, if not for you, Master, who else could do so?
The Master rose with a flourish and ascended the hall. He said, "'This very mind is Buddha'—this is like the ox from Jiazhou eating [grass]."

“Grain. Neither mind nor Buddha. “The horse in Yizhou has a bloated belly; it is neither mind nor Buddha. “Seeking a physician throughout the world, one applies moxibustion to the left shoulder of a pig.
After a long while: “Crying until the blood flows is of no use; it is better to keep one’s mouth shut and pass through the remainder of spring.
Ascending the hall, he said: “Sound is not sound; this is the Samādhi of Avalokiteśvara. Form is not form; this is the Dharma-gate of Mañjuśrī.”
Unimpeded by sound or form: this is the realm of Samantabhadra. Holding up his staff and drawing a line, he said: "The great garuḍa spreads its wings, covering the ten continents;
the swallows and sparrows by the hedge chirp in vain. He passed away at the age of sixty-seven, with fifty-five years of monastic seniority.
Chan Master Dishen Diyuan of Husheng Monastery in Taizhou was a native of Linhai.
While he was still a lay scholar, he paid his respects to his uncle, the Venerable Jian, at Baozang Temple in the village. By chance, he read the *Śūraṅgama Sūtra* on his uncle’s desk;

when he reached the passage stating that "the mountains, rivers, and the great earth are all objects manifested within the wondrously luminous mind," he set down the scroll and reflected upon its meaning for a long time, until suddenly—*huo*.
However, he experienced an awakening and requested permission from his parents to leave the household life. He took Jizhao as his teacher and donned the robes of a dhūta practitioner.
Over time, he became increasingly diligent. He emerged into the world to protect the sacred [Dharma] and later retired to the Eastern Hall for seven years.
There he composed several works, including the *Dayu Huanhai*, the *Fayun Tonglue*, the *Zuitan*, the *Wushuo*, and the *Rushi Jinghua*, totaling several volumes. Furthermore...
He composed the "Fu on the Great Lineage of Buddhas and Patriarchs. At the end of his life, he was forty-three years old.
Chan Master Chizhun of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou sent this verse for Attendant Zhong:
"When Niaoke blew up the cloth-hair, The attendant attained enlightenment on the spot. A pair of unperforated iron hammers— They dally with the arts of ghosts."

Consider this: if one is a truly sharp and discerning master, possessing a natural and innate air of dignity, they will expand the majestic light of their original ground and manifest the very core of the patch-robed monk.
They will encompass the great trichiliocosm within the tip of a single hair and fit Mount Sumeru into a mustard seed;
they walk directly upon the crown of Vairocana’s head, and even the Great Compassionate One with a thousand hands cannot restrain them.
Chan Master Zhongyou Zuchan of Tiantong Monastery in Ningbo Prefecture was also known by the sobriquet Guian. His clan name was Chen, and he was a native of Yinzhou.
He received the tonsure under Chan Master Kuang of Fozhi at Yongle and attained the essential meaning of the teaching while studying under Jizhao at Mount Jing.

After a long period, he emerged from seclusion at Lushan, subsequently moved to Xiangshan, and ascended to the position of abbot at Tiantong Monastery in the prefecture. On ascending the hall, he said: [The discourse follows].
A single phrase: the Buddhas of the three periods of time cannot speak it; the six generations of patriarchs cannot speak it;
the old monks of the world cannot speak it; this mountain monk cannot speak it; the great assembly cannot speak it. (He raises his staff.
Even if this staff could speak, that would still be the second phrase. Ascending the hall: "The very mind is Buddha; neither mind nor Buddha. It is not the mind.
"Not a Buddha. On Mount Wutai, clouds steam rice; before the steps of the Buddha Hall, it is a 'dog-urine sky.
At the top of the flagpole, *zhui* seeds are being fried; three monkeys toss coins at night. Ascending the hall on the Lantern Festival:
"Before the fifteenth day, head and tail are golden lotuses; after the fifteenth day, white oxen and tabby cats run in packs. Right now—
On the fifteenth day, the upper and lower levels of the pavilions were illuminated by fire; carriages and horses passed back and forth, and people gazed upon one another.
"A fine assembly! But tell me, in what way is it 'fine'? His eyes could not be deceived. He then descended from his seat.
The Single Mountain at the Heart of the Yangtze River: The Dharma Heir of Chan Master Wan.
Chan Master Baoen Wufang Zhipu was a native of Guiyang. His secular surname was Long. While presiding at the rear hall, he ascended the dais and said:
"In the sixth month, those who travel on the road spit smoke; they toil only because they are dragged by profit and fame. How can they compare to the disinterested guest beneath the forest trees?"
Awakening once, he slept with his robes until dawn. Striking the meditation seat, he rose and said, "Ganming does not begrudge his verbal karma; let me explain it for you:
on the thirtieth day of the twelfth month, Old Man Yan will demand from you the payment for your meals. He then ascended the hall and said: "The spring colors are thick; the spring days are bright.
The gardens are warm, and the wild peach blossoms are red. In the past, Lingyun saw this once and was liberated from form."
It is empty. Yet all people see it clearly; why then do they not awaken? If they do not awaken, their eyes will be caged by forms.

Tianning could not help but provide instruction so that they might attain awakening and entry. (He strikes the whisk. To teach people mistakenly is to cause them to resent the wind at the fifth watch.
The Great Zen Master Xiaoyin of Yunju in Nankang sat upright in his quarters all day long, appearing as serene as still water.
After his hair and beard were shaved, the attendants plucked out the remaining growths and scrambled to preserve them; as soon as they were removed, śarīra relics immediately appeared.
He once composed a verse for the Zen practitioner Xin, saying: "Faith is the mother of merit on the Way; If a medicine proves effective, it needs not be taken in great quantity. [End of Excerpt]
If a person can directly accept and take responsibility for this, what can even the Buddhas and Patriarchs do to them?
The Dharma Successor of Chan Master Yunfeng Gao of Mount Jing:
Chan Master Guzhi Zhe of Donglin, Jiangzhou. He was a native of Duchang and his secular surname was Chao. Initially, he resided at Xing...
Guo Xingsheng moved to Donglin. He ascended the hall and said: "The Buddhas of the past have already spoken; the Buddhas of the future shall speak;
the Buddhas of the present are speaking now. But ultimately, what is it they say? He struck his staff and descended from the seat. He ascended the hall again.
When clarity comes, darkness departs; when wisdom arises, delusion perishes. A black ox lies dead by the water; a mangy horse is tethered to a withered post.

How does this compare to the old Black Wang of East Village, who at dusk stretches out his legs to sleep and wakes only when the light of dawn appears? When I, this mountain monk, speak thus, it is like this.
Be most careful not to misunderstand. [Ascending the hall: I have fully taken up the guiding thread; neither sages nor ordinary beings can fathom it.

Now I loosen the path for all to tread, inviting you fellow practitioners to join me. A fragrant breeze blows from the south, bringing a subtle coolness to the halls and pavilions. [Ascending the hall: O virtuous Chan practitioners! The Patriarch said:
"Perfectly identical to the great void, with nothing lacking and nothing in excess. Beneath the three-beamed roof and before the seven-foot mat, be most careful not to rely on...
He gave this explanation: "Is there anyone who does not stick their head out beyond the heavens? He then said, "Circumambulate the hall and drink tea.
Regarding the verse for paying respects at the stupa of Chan Master Xian, he said: "The skull has always possessed its own numinous light; How could Xuedou ever have shaken out his entrails?
Having cut off the three-inch tongue of the old woman, To this day, the two swords lean against the sky, long and vast. [This was] sent to the Chan practitioner Wan as he went to visit Jingshan.
Venerable Xugou’s verse says: Ten thousand tracks and a thousand paths are on the same carriage; The eye of one who travels for study is correct and never errs.
Lord among fifteen hundred men, He was originally the Little Śākyamuni of Mount Yang.
○ Chan Master Shizhu of Yixi in Zhong Tianzhi, Hangzhou, was a native of Fujian.
When the Yuan troops descended upon the south of the Yangtze River, the Master, being young, was captured by marauding soldiers and brought to Lin’an; they then abandoned him and departed.

A wealthy man of the Hu family took him in and raised him, ordering him to accompany his own children and grandchildren to study at a local school. The Master would stand in a corner, concentrating his spirit and listening quietly, memorizing everything silently.
What had been lost was recovered, and the Hu family rejoiced. Once their son had grown up, they ordained him as a monk at Wuxiang Temple in their village.

He studied under Yunfeng at Mount Jing and attained the essential meaning [of the Dharma]. His observance of the precepts was refined and strict; his dharma robes and alms bowl never left his person. Initially, he resided at Wanshou Temple in Zhejiang.
Later, the Huang family of high standing, who deeply respected his spiritual conduct, frequently provided him with *kaṣāya* (vegetarian) offerings.

He served the meal. One day, he invited [the Master] back to his home to present offerings with even greater diligence; he then opened his private treasury and displayed the gold and jade to the Master, wishing to move his heart.
Upon returning, the Master said to those around him, "That Huang family displayed the treasures from their treasury to me, desiring to entice me to leave this life and become their son.
Little did they know that I regard gold and jade as mere rubble."
In ancient times, many fell into this same trap—not only for the sake of their sons, but there were even those who did so for the sake of their oxen and horses.
From this point on, I shall distance myself from the Huang family. At the beginning of the Tianli era, Xiaoyin of India was summoned by imperial decree to inaugurate the Great Longxiang Monastery;
when three candidates were proposed to succeed him as abbot of Zhongzhu Monastery, the Emperor’s brush marked the Master’s name. [The Xuanzheng...]
The monastery prepared a formal petition to earnestly invite him. After a long time, he passed away; accounts of his spiritual transformations and miraculous deeds were numerous.
*Zen Master Benyuan Shanda of Mount Jing in Hangzhou:* He was of the Chai clan of Xianju.
In his youth, he traveled with Jigan Xin, vowing never to hold official monastic office. He went to Jiangxi to see Xueyan at Yangshan, where he entered the master’s room along with the assembly.
He had no further insights to report. Later, he returned to Xianju, where the local people requested him to preside over Duofu Temple.

He declined and traveled to Hunan to preside over Foyan Temple. Subsequently, he returned to Zhejiang to visit Yunfeng at Mount Jing; upon entering the master’s room for instruction, he attained realization. Yunfeng certified his attainment.
Coincidentally, as the seat of Huiyun was vacant, the master was appointed to fill it. Later, he resided at Baoning, Jingci, and Mount Jing, achieving distinguished success at each.
This is worthy of record. Wherever the Master resided, he did not provide a bed; at night, he would burn incense, light candles, and sit upright until dawn, making this his constant practice.

○ Chan Master Dingweng Nai of Gushan, Fuzhou, ascended the hall for the discourse.
Before the drum had even sounded, the ancient Buddha was manifest in full majesty. As soon as the drum sounded, Śākyamuni entered right through everyone’s nostrils. Mí...
Le leaps into the eyes of all people. Do you still feel the heaviness at the crown of your head?
Chan Master Nanzhou Zhen of Wanshou Monastery in Suzhou first resided at Nengren in Changshu, then moved to Kaixian on Mount Lu, and finally ascended to Wanshou.
He entered the hall and said: "The Great Way is right before one's eyes, yet it is difficult to behold even there."
If you wish to recognize the true essence of the Great Way, it is not separate from sound, form, and speech. It is the very ground you tread upon, the bricks and tiles beneath your feet;
it is the lanterns and pillars you encounter. Ultimately, where does the true essence of the Great Way reside? After a long silence, he descended from his seat.

Ascending the hall, [the Master] said: "If the eye does not sleep, all dreams are naturally eliminated; if the mind does not vary, the myriad dharmas are of one suchness. Great assembly, what do you call the 'sleepless eye'?
What do you call the 'unvarying mind'? After a long silence, he said: "The snow is spun into thread and the mulberry trees turn green again;
the golden clouds are harvested and the rice is now a vibrant green. Ascending the hall, he said: "Till the soil and eat; raise silkworms and wear clothes."

In the creative transformation of heaven and earth, the myriad things are born through the four seasons. What need is there to speak of "no cultivation and no realization," or "no-thought and non-action"?
This mountain monk will be seventy-three years old next year; who would have known that one born in the year of the Ox (Biyou) does not belong to the Rooster?

○ Fourth is Master Dingshui Baoye Yuan of Mingzhou, a native of his own prefecture. He studied under Xutang at Mount Jing;
whenever there were matters regarding the kōans of the Zen school that he could not penetrate, he would invariably consult the elder master for resolution. One day, he asked Xutang:
Regarding Deshan’s final word: if one says it exists, how could Deshan have failed to realize it? If one says it does not exist, yet Yantou further stated that Deshan had not yet realized it.
I hope the Venerable Master will compassionately provide instruction. The Abbot said, "I do not know; go and ask Chief Seat Yun. The Master went to ask Yun.
It happened that Yun had just returned from a mountain excursion and was asking for water to wash his feet. The Master respectfully advanced with the water.
He threw himself down and reached out his hands to rub and stroke [the feet]. Then, looking up, he asked, "I do not yet know whether Master Deshan’s final word exists or not;
I hope the Head Seat will grant me an instruction. Yunzhu took both hands, scooped up the water for washing the feet, and splashed it over him.
"What is the final phrase? The Master did not understand its meaning. The next day, he went to see the Abbot (Dongshan) and recounted the matter of his questioning Yunmen in full.
The Abbot said, "He had no other words. The Master said, "He asked, 'What is the final phrase? The Abbot said, "That is it; I will tell you that he understood.
At that moment, the Master was suddenly relieved. Later, while residing [there], a monk asked him, "Do you remember the monk's question?"
Dongshan was asked, "What is the Buddha? Dongshan replied, "Three pounds of flax. "What is the meaning of this? The Master said, "The confession comes from the prisoner's own mouth.
Another monk asked, "And how about Zhaozhou’s answer when he was asked, 'What is the Buddha? Zhaozhou said, 'The one in the hall. What does that mean?
The Master said, "Buying high and selling low. He ascended the hall and said: "When seeing is seen, that which sees is not the seeing. Seeing...
It is like being beyond the reach of views; views cannot attain it. The Master held up his staff and said, "The Old Śākyamuni has stepped firmly upon the four corners of the earth.
Is there anyone who can save him? He let out a shout. Ascending the hall, he said: "When you draw your feet back onto the meditation seat, there is no such thing as staying forever without walking.
When you carry the staff across your shoulder, there is no such thing as walking forever without stopping. Abandoning that place to come here—from the West, one passes through."

To the east, there is absolutely nothing of the Buddha-dharma to disturb the mind, nor is there anything of worldly convention to dwell upon. With coarse rice and plain soup, one passes the days according to conditions;

with incense burners and tea bowls, one finds satisfaction as the occasion arises. How can a single phrase repay the debt of gratitude? Through what means can it be struck and chanted? When the wind ceases, the sky of Yao is vast;
when the clouds part, the sun of Shun shines bright. Ascending the hall, he raised the case: Once, a monk asked Master Zhaozhou, "What is..."
Regarding the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West, Master Shou said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. A monk said, "Master, do not point to external objects to show people.
Shou said, "I am not pointing to external objects to show you. The monk asked, "What is the meaning of the Patriarch’s coming from the West?
Shou said, "The cypress tree in the courtyard. The Master [Zhaozhou] commented: "Before this monk had even raised his question, he was already steeped in dark blue."
"Two thousand *chi* high. Zhaozhou answered once more. "How could it be merely that its frost-battered bark and rain-soddened trunk measure forty spans in circumference?
Entering the hall, he said: "In all quarters, people talk of Chan with great clamor, yet at Chongfu there is no clarity whatsoever. With faces covered in dust and heads grey with age, time passes;
the duties of the abbot are not fulfilled. His arms are long while his robe sleeves are too short; his *zhiduo* and *kāṣāya* are coarse cloth and dark gray. Taking what is non-existent..."

"Fame and profit are entirely left behind by the horse-riding guest; right and wrong do not reach the fisherman."
Chan Master Lingshi Ruizhi of Jingci Monastery in Hangzhou first resided at Xingsheng Monastery in Jiahe, then moved to Yongquan in Tiantai and Benjue in Jiaxing.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: "A solitary wasp cannot transform a bean caterpillar; a cock from Lu cannot hatch a swan’s egg.
Within these ninety days, a patch-robed monk must insist on steaming sand to make rice—this half and that half."

'The entire earth has not a single hair’s breadth of affliction—this is still a turning phrase. Not seeing a single color is only half the presentation.'"

Furthermore, you must know that there is a time for the total presentation. [He] strikes the meditation staff and descends from the seat. Ascending the hall: It has been one month since the summer retreat began;
the passage of time flows as swiftly as a rushing torrent. The water-buffalo grazes on sweet grass and water; Hanshan, having eaten his fill, plays with his chopsticks.
To mend the vital organs and rouse chronic ailments, this mountain monk has a simple and private prescription to bestow upon all of you. [He] strikes the whisk.
My son, when eating or drinking, measure the place from which it comes.
Master Xixian of Lingyan’s Bamboo Window ascended the hall and said: "Every day, as you all walk, stand, sit, and lie down; as you hear, see, perceive, and know;
as you bow, look up, turn, and move; as you reach out, lean, respond, and engage—every single point is the perfect fusion of wondrous function, and every place is the radiance of the divine spirit."
Complete! When you hear the sound of the bell, you put on your robes; when you hear the sound of the drum, you ascend the hall.

If you can see clearly here, I grant you seven holes and eight apertures. Otherwise, ten thousand purples and a thousand reds will all wither away, and the spring of the year will have come to naught once more.
Master Xuedou Yuxi Yu of Siming ascended the hall and said: "What is the Buddha? 'The very mind is the Buddha'—if you understand it this way, it is not so.
What is the Buddha? 'The very mind is the Buddha'—only when you understand it this way is it so."
Gold does not barter for gold; water does not wash water. Two or three rows of hawks against the cold clouds; seven or eight leaves of reeds within the autumn colors.

Chan Master Jingfu of Huyan at Mount Jingshan in Hangzhou was a native of Huai’an. Initially serving as the head seat at Zhongtianzhu, he later took up residence at Shishuang in Tanzhou.
Upon ascending the hall, he said: “Vast and empty, without reliance—what kind of realm is this?

The wind does not rustle the branches; the rain does not break the clods of earth. Striking the meditation seat with his whisk, he said: “Even the reigns of Emperors Yao and Shun still left traces of their transformation.”
Ascending the hall: "This phrase, not this phrase; full presentation, partial presentation. Carving out hollows in empty space; branches sprouting from the joints of a tree.

For such an illness as this, there is nothing wrong with being struck three thousand times in the morning and eight hundred times in the evening. Ascending the hall: To receive the intent before the pivot;
to clarify the source beneath the phrase. Yunmen was pressed until his feet were broken; Baizhang was shouted at until his ears went deaf. Fallen flowers.

Rain in the third month; the fifth-watch bell amidst lingering dreams. Entering the hall, he said: "Picking incense, selecting fire, drawing water, and carrying wood—these are not the wondrous functioning of spiritual powers.
Putting on clothes, eating food, defecating, urinating, and attending to one's needs—these are not the wondrous functioning of spiritual powers.
But what, after all, is it? "Leisurely and expansive, always like a simpleton; there is naturally someone who understands him. Entering the hall, he lit the lamp.
"If you go directly beneath his heels, I shall give you thirty blows. If you do not move, he will turn you over onto your crown; even then, you would still be lacking a single stroke.
If you do none of these things—'How many kinds of cloud colors emerge from the mountain peak? How uniform is the sound of the spring falling before the railing? Ascending the hall, [the Master said:
'A stone falling from a high mountain naturally exhausts its momentum upon reaching level ground; waves arising in the great ocean cease when they encounter windless waters.'"
The waves subside of their own accord. When both ends are cut off and not a single dharma remains, where is there brightness or darkness, form or emptiness?
Where are there mountains, rivers, and the great earth? Nevertheless, this is not the hand of monk You; it is merely speaking of being skilled in painting. Ascending the hall:
At the summit of Lingxiao Peak, there is a large chessboard stone—neither square nor round, neither level nor slanted.
Oblique. It cannot be lifted or grasped; it cannot be pierced or dissected. Moss and ivy envelop it without entanglement; wind, rain, mist, and clouds wash over it without wetting it.
Taking the myriad stars and constellations and the ten thousand phenomena of the universe as a single set of chess pieces, they appear during the bright moon and vanish during the dark moon.
From antiquity to the present, no one has ever made a single move. The patch-robed monks stand by...
Contemplating the "having-parts" (bhavāṅga). The mountain monk shall attempt to provide one stroke for you. He suddenly takes up his staff, strikes once, and says:
"The path is perilous where it is level; people are busy amidst stillness."
○ Chan Master Shizhong, the "Ordinary Old Man" (Yongsou) of Chengtian Temple in Suzhou, first studied under Wuzhun at Mount Jing.
Subsequently, he met Xuzhou at Lengquan. When he appeared in the world at Wannian Temple in Siming to open the hall and offer incense, he said:

Once that fellow sniffed him, he was left breathless, his vitality entirely gone, leaving a scent that permeated heaven and scorched the earth. Thus it is said:
He said: "Ascending the hall: To be without mind is a deviation; to apply intention is an error. How does a skilled physician dispense medicine?
[He] pats his knee once and says: 'Muzhou carries a board; Puhua shakes his bell. Ascending the hall, he cites a monk asking Yunmen:

The Master’s verse says: "The spring scenery is everywhere, never partial; White and red flowers each display their own beauty.

"Śākyamuni Buddha spent forty-nine years preaching, yet he could not say it all. Bodhidharma sat in cold meditation for nine years, yet he could not see through it."
It cannot be described, nor can it be seen through. The Sea God knows its nobility but not its price; it remains for the world to illuminate the night.

"Yet within affairs, one penetrates to the state of no-affairs; seeing forms and hearing sounds, one does not become deaf. O Great Assembly!

The water flows from the east. Ascending the hall, he said: "Three parts of time have already passed; when has it ever been moved?

This is also the place of ordinary conduct. If one does not turn back when called, what can be done? There is no predecessor before and no successor behind. Chengtian speaks thus."

Wan bowed. Zhoudue said, "An understanding such as this does not depart from the teachings. As the Master prepared to reply, Zhoudue struck him across the face with his fist.

In the Wushen year of the Zhide era, he moved to Tiantong. Upon ascending the hall, he said: "In the place of stillness, there is a vast clamor; in the midst of clamor, there is profound stillness. Be careful, O practitioners!"

the rustic elder knows nothing of the labors of Yao and Shun. 'Today three, tomorrow four'—thus one idly passes through one's youth."
